title: Digital Transformation Readiness and user Acceptance of an Integrated Management Information System in a Public HEI in Northern Mindanao
affiliations: Northern Bukidnon State College, Northern Bukidnon State College, Northern Bukidnon State College, Northern Bukidnon State College and Northern Bukidnon State College

detail.title: Digital Transformation Readiness and user Acceptance of an Integrated Management Information System in a Public HEI in Northern Mindanao

declarations.funderStatement: Regular Research Fund of Northern Bukidnon State College

detail.abstract: Digital transformation in higher education requires institutions to assess organizational readiness and user acceptance before implementing complex information systems such as an Integrated Management Information System (IMIS). This study evaluates the readiness of Northern Bukidnon State College for IMIS adoption using a descriptive-evaluative quantitative design. Data were collected through a structured survey administered to 100 active faculty and administrative personnel who regularly use the institution’s existing integrated system. Guided by the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, the study analyzed user perceptions of system usability, functionality, and facilitating conditions. Findings revealed high levels of perceived usefulness (M = 4.30) and ease of use (M = 4.31), indicating strong user acceptance of the current system. Technical support and responsiveness were also rated positively, reflecting favorable institutional support. However, training and structured orientation received a low exposure rating (M = 0.63), highlighting a significant gap in operational readiness and workforce preparation. Regression analysis further showed that facilitating conditions, particularly training-related support, significantly influence user satisfaction and system acceptance. Overall, the findings suggest that NBSC demonstrates partial readiness for IMIS implementation. While technical and usability foundations are well established, successful digital transformation will depend on strengthening structured training, user orientation, and institutional capacity building initiatives.

title: Latent Structure Recognition: A Testable Operator Variable in Multi-Turn Human-AI Interaction

detail.title: Latent Structure Recognition: A Testable Operator Variable in Multi-Turn Human-AI Interaction

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or identifiable personal information.

detail.abstract: Large language model performance is usually evaluated as a property of the model, the prompt, the task, or the surrounding system architecture. Extended human-AI interaction introduces another variable: the human operator. This paper proposes Latent Structure Recognition (LSR) as a measurable operator-side capacity relevant to multiturn AI performance. LSR is defined as the ability to infer the governing structure of an unfolding interaction from incomplete observable evidence, detect meaningful deviation from that structure before overt failure occurs, and introduce corrective information that restores task fidelity without adding unnecessary noise. The framework makes no claim of access to hidden model states, latent representations, chain-of-thought, machine consciousness, or supernatural intuition. The operator observes behavior, infers structure, and acts on that inference. The inference may be right or wrong. Recognition inside an adaptive system is not passive. Once an operator acts on an inferred structure, the intervention changes what happens next. The operator may therefore recognize an emerging structure, induce it, or participate in a coupled process containing both effects. LSR treats that ambiguity as an empirical problem rather than assuming the answer. The framework extends prior work on interaction-level coherence by specifying a candidate human-side mechanism. In this account, the operator can function as an external coherence regulator: detecting deviation, transmitting correction, evaluating uptake, and preserving a governing coordinate across turns. The Engineering question is direct: Can the regulatory advantages of a high-LSR operator be transferred to users who do not naturally possess them?

title: Disentangling the Measurement of Uncertainty from Risk
affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Shanghai Advanced Institute of Finance (SAIF), Fudan University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU)

detail.title: Disentangling the Measurement of Uncertainty from Risk
detail.abstract: This paper disentangles Knightian uncertainty from risk within the location-scale (LS) family, where uncertainty and risk are governed, respectively, by the LS set and random seeds with standard probability distributions. Extending classical stochasticdominance arguments, we establish that neither a unanimous ranking nor any scalar, preference-independent measure of uncertainty exists in general for broad classes of utility functions, thereby identifying fundamental limits of uncertainty quanti…cation. Nevertheless, we show that the mean-average characteristic function provides a partial order that never contradicts the unanimous ranking whenever it is attainable. For rectangular LS sets and Gaussian normal random seeds, the upper and lower bounds of LS parameters can be fully identi…ed by the …rst, second, fourth, and sixth mean-average moments, yielding tractable partial assessment of uncertainty. We further propose a composite uncertainty measure grounded in the concentration-of-measure phenomenon, o¤ering a complementary partial assessment. An empirical illustration using daily open, high, low, and close prices of the S&P 500 demonstrates that uncertainty is distinct from risk and has pricing implications not captured by traditional risk measures. The results o¤er theoretically justi…ed and empirically tractable tools for robust decision making under uncertainty.

title: GenAI Recommendation Agents and Consumer Satisfaction in Online Reviews: Evidence from Online Travel Agency
affiliations: Harbin Institute of Technology, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - Department of Information Systems, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) and The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: GenAI Recommendation Agents and Consumer Satisfaction in Online Reviews: Evidence from Online Travel Agency
detail.abstract: GenAI recommendation agents (GenAI RAs) are rapidly being adopted across e-commerce platforms to interactively provide highly personalized product recommendations. Yet their impact on consumer satisfaction, reflected in review ratings and rating polarization, remains unclear, despite its central role in platform performance and consumer decision-making. Leveraging a platform-scale natural experiment around a leading online travel agency's adoption of GenAI RA, we construct a matched multi-platform panel of U.S. hotel reviews from Expedia, Booking.com, and Hotels.com and estimate causal effects using difference-indifferences models. We find that GenAI RA adoption increases average review ratings while amplifying rating polarization. This polarization is asymmetric: high ratings increase substantially, low ratings rise modestly, and mid-range ratings decline, suggesting that while GenAI RAs yield a net positive benefit, they also lead to dissatisfaction among some consumers. Drawing on needs fulfillment theory, we propose that GenAI RAs enhance product-need fit by eliciting consumers' self-relevant needs through conversational interaction, thereby improving satisfaction. Textual analyses of review content provide supporting evidence for the mechanism. Reviewers exhibit greater cognitive engagement and shift their review structures toward greater attribute-level depth but narrower breadth, focusing more extensively on their self-relevant needs. Crucially, high-rating reviews show greater cognitive engagement and detailed needs descriptions, while low-rating reviews reflect stronger emotional expression and reduced analytical depth, indicating dissatisfaction when needs are unmet. Furthermore, hotel star ratings serve as a boundary condition: GenAI RAs boost ratings more effectively for lower-star hotels but intensify polarization for higher-star hotels, suggesting more effective fulfillment of lower-order needs but greater heterogeneity in higher-order needs. This study identifies GenAI RAs as a key driver of the level and distribution of satisfaction, while demonstrating how they reshape the cognitive-affective and structural dimensions of reviews. It extends needs fulfillment theory to conversational recommendation and offers managerial insights for platform governance and GenAI adoption.

title: When Output Stops Being Evidence Generative AI and Production-Verification Decoupling in Institutional Accountability

detail.title: When Output Stops Being Evidence Generative AI and Production-Verification Decoupling in Institutional Accountability
detail.abstract: Institutions have long relied on an unspoken filter: producing convincing work was difficult enough that doing it well was itself evidence of competence. Generative AI collapses that cost, and with it the filter, leaving institutions unable to tell from output alone whether the person behind it understood anything. This article develops the concept of production-verification decoupling to name the resulting condition and to explain why it strikes some settings hard and others barely at all. The article is a theory-building synthesis rather than an empirical study, and it treats its sources accordingly, resting the mechanisms on peer-reviewed work and using industry and journalistic material only to illustrate emerging practice. It distinguishes two scales. At the institutional scale, decoupling has two conditions: proxy collapse, a loss of the ability to read competence from output, and generation-verification asymmetry, a loss of the capacity to check output at volume. At the interactional scale, repeated exchange between a user and a model produces epistemic entrainment, a coupling that stabilises a conversational frame without independent verification and whose outputs then enter institutional decision chains as though independently checked. The claims are stated as four testable propositions rather than estimated models. A governance heuristic, the Macbeth-Hamlet corridor, maps the space between over-trusting AI output and over-verifying it, and a cross-sector comparison identifies where verification needs to be redesigned deliberately and where existing mechanisms already absorb the shock.

detail.abstract: Enterprise digital transformation initiatives exhibit persistently high failure rates—industry surveys consistently report rates above 70%, and this has remained stubbornly stable despite sustained global IT spending. The fundamental cause is not technological inadequacy but a structural longitudinal disconnect among business decision-making, architectural design, and project execution: strategic intent attenuates and feedback loops break down across these layers, leaving enterprises in the predicament of "money spent, systems built, value not realized." Grounded in design science research (Hevner et al., 2004), this study develops the MAP (Management–Architecture–Project) three-layer integrated governance model, in which the Business-Architecture Interface (BAI) and the Architecture-Project Interface (API) enable bidirectional verification: BAI empowers the architecture layer to veto unrealistic business assumptions, while API lets execution reality correct architectural design. A ten-penetration-line governance checklist (core general, digital-enhancement, and cross-border stress lines) operationalizes the model into an auditable, quantifiable tool. A demonstration scenario of New Zealand dairy digital transformation validates logical consistency and mechanism completeness; the same governance failure logic applies across asset-intensive, asset-light, and public-sector settings. Contribution. The study extends strategic alignment theory from cross-sectional to longitudinal governance, brings boundary-object theory (Star & Griesemer, 1989) into intra-organizational cross-layer governance, and positions the governance-failure diagnosis as a governance turn in IS failure research—providing a context-agnostic framework compatible with international standards (TOGAF, PMBOK, ISO series).

title:
Crystal Memory for Native Character-Identity Streams 
Local Retrieval, Cycle-Bound Retention, and the Boundary of Causal Learning

detail.title:
Crystal Memory for Native Character-Identity Streams 
Local Retrieval, Cycle-Bound Retention, and the Boundary of Causal Learning
detail.abstract: NINMENI represents each character as one immutable identity unit (NMU): one character, one ID, and one causal state event. This paper specifies the crystal memory used by the active 98,127,393-parameter VEYRA NYRA TRAIN_0002 revision. The mechanism is a bounded per-stream numerical state, not a symbolic lexicon: 64 slots of width 768, a non-negative mass per slot, and a last-write position. A write opportunity occurs at a globally aligned rhythm of 512 character events. Valid within-segment states are summarized with Emylton-derived weights, projected into one candidate crystal, and assigned to the least-mass slot after cycle-bound retention. Retrieval uses K1-C Local Iso-Capacity: every occupied slot receives a query-local gate with no normalization across slots, after which local contributions are aggregated. RH-K0 initializes the retention factor to a 64-write half-life, giving an exact nominal half-life of 32,768 character events at the frozen write rhythm for a slot that is neither rewritten nor evicted. Three-seed mechanical probes establish output/state/gradient parity of the K1 primitive, bounded finite retrieval, 64 cold fills followed by 16 evictions over 80 writes per seed, and finite nonzero routes to the query and retention parameters. A separate actual-parameter probe establishes finite gradients, post-clipping signal, and nonzero AdamW parameter deltas on a revision-bound research path. Checkpoint-500 evidence establishes loadability, mechanism identity, finite model and optimizer tensors, and separate telemetry for Emylton PB-K0 state and PBAN O5 learning-action state. These results establish mechanical operation and provenance. They do not establish that a slot is a word, sentence, proposition, or concept; nor do they establish knowledge, generalization, tool-use competence, or output quality.

title: Latent Liquidity and Structural Mass: A State-Based Theory of Hidden Capacity, Replenishment, and Executable Market Support

detail.title: Latent Liquidity and Structural Mass: A State-Based Theory of Hidden Capacity, Replenishment, and Executable Market Support
detail.abstract: Electronic order books reveal only a portion of the liquidity capable of influencing price formation. Displayed depth may vanish before contact, while apparently thin markets may repeatedly absorb aggressive flow through reserve size, rapid same-price replenishment, crossvenue response, or strategic re-entry. This paper develops a state-based theory of latent liquidity and structural mass for electronic markets. It defines latent liquidity as executable or potentially executable capacity that is not fully represented by the contemporaneous displayed book, and structural mass as the behaviorally weighted combination of persistent displayed liquidity and empirically supported latent capacity that remains relevant to local price resistance. The framework does not equate every replenishment event with an iceberg order, nor does it infer hidden intent from a static heatmap. Instead, latent capacity must be earned as an inference through repeated execution contact, replenishment timing, queue continuity, persistence, pricecoordinate stability, and out-of-sample explanatory power. The theory distinguishes six forms of non-immediate capacity: exchange-defined reserve liquidity, replenishment-linked latent mass, reactive re-entry, migrating liquidity, cross-venue latent support, and model-implied latent demand or supply. It introduces a Latent Capacity Vector, Structural Mass Index, Latency-to-Replenishment distribution, Absorption Persistence Score, and an uncertainty-adjusted Latent-Mass Confidence measure. These constructs are integrated with Liquidity Commitment Theory, Market State Dynamics, Liquidity Commitment Cascades, and Liquidity Recovery and Market Hysteresis. The principal prediction is that price susceptibility depends not only on visible depth but also on the durability and location of inferred structural mass. Two books with equal displayed quantity may therefore exhibit materially different impact, recovery, and secondary-collapse risk. The paper proposes falsifiable tests using exchange-sequenced market-by-order data, execution episodes, reserve-order flags where available, cross-venue synchronization, and matched controls. It specifies conditions under which latent-mass claims should be rejected, narrowed, or treated only as reduced-form estimates. The contribution is a disciplined bridge between visible orderbook measurement and the broader executable capacity that becomes observable only through time. Latent liquidity is treated neither as mystical hidden supply nor as a license for retrospective storytelling, but as an uncertain state variable that must be estimated, validated, and reported with explicit confidence bounds.

title: The Hand-Off Readiness Score: A Formative Measurement Model for Information Loss at IT Project Phase Boundaries

detail.title: The Hand-Off Readiness Score: A Formative Measurement Model for Information Loss at IT Project Phase Boundaries

declarations.ethicsApproval: This is a conceptual measurement-design paper. It does not report the results of an empirical study involving patients, human participants, personal data, surveys, interviews, focus groups, experiments, or animal subjects. No instrument described in this paper was administered to any respondent, and no pilot, validation, or calibration data were collected. All evidence used is drawn from published peer-reviewed literature, systematic reviews, methodological guidance, and openly accessible scholarly sources, and is cited accordingly. No primary data were collected from identifiable individuals, and no confidential or personal information was obtained or analysed. Consequently, no review or approval from an institutional ethics committee, institutional review board (IRB), or equivalent body was required for this work. No case-study consent was necessary, as the paper does not present individual case studies of identifiable persons or organisations. The author notes that the empirical validation programme set out in Section VIII will involve human participants, will collect data on live project boundaries within organisations, and will therefore require institutional ethics approval, informed participant consent, and organisational data-sharing agreements before any step beyond Step 4 is undertaken. No such work has been carried out at the time of writing. The author has no competing interests and no external funding sources to declare in relation to this paper.

detail.abstract: A prior systematic review of forty-eight studies on information loss at IT project phase boundaries identified five research gaps, of which two are foundational: the absence of a standardised inter-phase hand-off protocol and the absence of a measurement model for information loss itself. The second gap blocks progress on the others, because a construct that cannot be measured cannot be linked causally to scope drift, defect density, or rework. This paper addresses that gap by specifying the Hand-Off Readiness Score, a formative index of the condition of a phase transition at the moment it occurs. The construct is defined as the degree to which a receiving phase team possesses the information, rationale, and decision authority required to proceed without reconstructing what the sending phase already knew. Six dimensions are derived from the review's thematic synthesis and from the structured hand-off literature in clinical medicine, where instruments such as I-PASS and SBAR have demonstrated measurable reductions in error rates: artefact completeness, rationale retention, traceability continuity, receiver comprehension, decision-authority clarity, and residual-ambiguity disclosure. The paper argues that the index must be specified as formative rather than reflective, because the dimensions are constitutive ingredients rather than interchangeable manifestations, and that it must be scored at the receiving boundary rather than the sending one, because a hand-off that the sender considers complete and the receiver cannot use is definitionally a failed hand-off. This receiver-side asymmetry is the paper's central design commitment and distinguishes the instrument from existing gate-review checklists, which certify sender output. A ten-step validation roadmap following established construct-development procedure is set out, together with the content-validity thresholds, collinearity diagnostics, and indicator-weight criteria appropriate to a formative specification. The paper states the conditions under which the construct would be judged to have failed, and positions the instrument for pilot validation in the Indian multi-vendor delivery context identified by the review as the least studied.

title: Homo Hospes: The Fourth Evolutionary Form of Humanity and Its Realization Path in the AGI Era
affiliations: HUMHOST AI PTE. LTD,  and HUMHOST AI PTE. LTD

detail.title: Homo Hospes: The Fourth Evolutionary Form of Humanity and Its Realization Path in the AGI Era
detail.abstract: As advanced general intelligence (AGI) progressively blurs the boundary betweenhuman cognition and digital systems, established evolutionary frameworks of humanity—exemplified by Homo sapiens, Homo economicus, and Homo deus—lackexplanatory power for an emerging symbiotic life form, in which humans retainfull autonomous agency while co-evolving with an embedded AI cognitive system. This paper formally conceptualizes Homo Hospes (the Fourth Human) as an original account of the fourth evolutionary form of humanity. Defined as a self-governing symbiotic life entity, Homo Hospes takes the individual human being as the biological host of an embedded AI cognitive system, and achieves unified self-awareness, autonomous agency, and co-evolution through the alignment of biological code, cognitive code, and digital code. The Agentor (humanized intelligent execution entity) serves as its core implementation carrier in organizational andproject scenarios. Grounded in the Three-Code Synergy framework at the individual level and the Six-Chain human-AI collaboration mechanism at the organizational level, this paper elaborates the core attributes, evolutionary stages, and actionable pathways of Homo Hospes. It further discusses its applied value in entrepreneurial incubation, expert capability upgrading, organizational innovation, and organizational symbiont construction, and proposes verifiable propositions for subsequent empirical investigation. This study extends the theoretical discourse on human evolution in the digital age, establishes a complete logical chain from individual cognitive upgrading to organizational capability iteration, and provides a systematic theoretical foundationfor human-centered AI empowerment practices.

title: The Sales Impact of Product Presentation in Live Streaming E-Commerce -A Narrative Transportation Perspective
affiliations: , City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - Department of Information Systems and The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: The Sales Impact of Product Presentation in Live Streaming E-Commerce -A Narrative Transportation Perspective
detail.abstract: In live streaming e-commerce, unlike static and impersonal e-commerce product displays, streamers present product information, expressions, and real-time social interaction to persuade consumers via a live video. Information systems researchers have addressed the sales impact of virtual product presentation, but there is limited understanding of how streamers' live video presentations can be structured to improve product sales. Extending narrative transportation theory to the context of live streaming e-commerce, we posit that the sales impact of presentation structure varies with its degree of narrativity, characterized by temporal embedding (i.e., verbal speech that organizes streamers' presentation activities of streamers in a temporal and causal sequence) and emotional volatility (i.e., moment-to-moment shifts between streamers' emotional valences as shown in facial expression). We incorporate two moderators that may alter the impact of narrativity: product trial, through which streamers interact with the product, and interaction prompt, through which they interact with the live streaming audience. Using a rich dataset of 3,850 product-level video clips from Taobao Live, we find that temporal embedding improves product sales only when the streamer demonstrates product usage in a product trial. Interestingly, emotional volatility exhibits a stronger positive effect on product sales with low product trial and low interaction prompt. We investigate how these findings contribute to the live streaming literature and narrative transportation theory, and discuss their practical implications for streamers and live streaming platform operators.

title: Financial Technology, Investment Management, and Capital Market Services

detail.title: Financial Technology, Investment Management, and Capital Market Services
detail.abstract:
Financial technology has reshaped the way capital is raised, invested, traded, and supervised. Innovations in electronic trading, algorithmic execution, digital advisory services, and distributed infrastructure have altered the structure of capital markets and the delivery of investment management services, while introducing new categories of operational, technological, and regulatory risk.

This research examines financial technology as it applies to investment management and capital market services. It considers the FinTech ecosystem and its participants, the digital transformation of primary and secondary markets, the risk management and cybersecurity implications of technology adoption, the governance and internal control frameworks required to oversee it, and the contribution of financial technology to financial inclusion. The study concludes with an assessment of the developments expected to shape investment management and capital market infrastructure over the coming decade.

title: Financial Technology Infrastructure

detail.title: Financial Technology Infrastructure
detail.abstract:
Financial markets increasingly depend upon sophisticated technological infrastructures that facilitate the efficient exchange of information, movement of funds, settlement of transactions, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity protection, and operational resilience. These foundational technologies serve as critical enablers of modern financial systems and support the stability, efficiency, and scalability of financial services globally.

This research examines the technological infrastructure underlying contemporary financial markets, with particular emphasis on financial market infrastructures, payment systems, cloud computing, data management, digital identity systems, cybersecurity frameworks, regulatory technologies, operational resilience, and emerging digital architectures. The study analyzes the role of infrastructure in enabling financial innovation while maintaining security, reliability, and market integrity. Furthermore, the research explores future developments that are expected to transform the architecture of financial systems over the coming decades.

title:
Digital Mobile Money in Ethiopia's Somali Region:

A Case Study of eBirr in Jijiga, with an Assessment of Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery

detail.title:
Digital Mobile Money in Ethiopia's Somali Region:

A Case Study of eBirr in Jijiga, with an Assessment of Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
detail.abstract: Digital mobile money has become one of the most consequential financial technologies in Sub-Saharan Africa, extending payment, savings, and transfer services to populations historically excluded from formal banking. Ethiopia entered this transformation later than East African peers such as Kenya and Tanzania, but liberalization of the payments sector after 2020 has allowed telecom-linked and bank-linked mobile financial service (MFS) providers, including eBirr, telebirr, and CBE Birr, to expand rapidly. This paper examines the diffusion and use of eBirr mobile money in Jijiga, the capital of Ethiopia's Somali Regional State, a peripheral, pastoralist, and partly conflict- and drought-affected area that also hosts refugee and host communities. The paper synthesizes secondary literature, provider documentation, and regional development-agency research to characterize adoption drivers and barriers among Somali-region users, and then turns to an organizational-resilience question that has received little attention in the mobile money literature: how well is eBirr's service in Jijiga positioned to maintain continuity of operations and to recover from disruption, whether from network outages, power failure, agent liquidity shocks, climatic hazards, or insecurity. Using a business continuity management (BCM) and disaster recovery (DR) framework adapted to a low-connectivity, agent-based financial service, the paper develops a risk register, a business impact analysis, and a set of continuity strategies suited to Jijiga's operating environment. Findings suggest that while eBirr's USSD-based, agent-dependent design gives it structural resilience against smartphone- and internet-dependent failure modes, it remains vulnerable to telecom network single points of failure, agent cash-liquidity shortages, low digital and financial literacy, and the compounding effects of drought and localized insecurity common to the Somali Region. The paper concludes with recommendations for eBirr, its banking and telecom partners, and regional regulators to strengthen continuity planning and disaster recovery capacity in fragile, refugee-hosting, and climateexposed markets.

title: Proportionate Traceability Data Requirements for Honey Fraud Deterrence: Core vs Tiered Assurance under Producer Heterogeneity
affiliations: University of Economics in Katowice, University of Economics in Katowice and University of Economics in Katowice

detail.title: Proportionate Traceability Data Requirements for Honey Fraud Deterrence: Core vs Tiered Assurance under Producer Heterogeneity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there is no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This non-invasive study involved only adult participants and did not require formal ethics committee approval under the institutional procedures of the University of Economics in Katowice. Data collection was conducted by an external research provider in compliance with ethical requirements and the GDPR.
declarations.funderStatement: The publication was developed within the #TOP4HoneyChains – Trustable and Sustainable Open Platform for Smart Honey Value Chains project, funded by #NCBR under the ERA-NET CO-FUND ICT-AGRI-FOOD initiative (ICTAGRIFOOD/II/67/TOP4HoneyChain/2023, 2023–2026), implemented under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 programme (Grant Agreement No. 862665).

detail.abstract:
Purpose-This study identifies which traceability data elements should be prioritized to deter honey fraud and support credible assurance and examines how producer heterogeneity shapes readiness for differentiated traceability requirements. 

Design/methodology/approach-An exploratory sequential mixed-methods design was employed. Expert interviews (n = 30) specified traceability data elements and their assurance roles; a survey of Polish beekeepers (n = 949) assessed perceived importance and producer characteristics. Survey analysis combined descriptive statistics, K-modes clustering, non-parametric between-cluster tests, and multinomial logistic regression. 

Findings-Experts structured traceability into four domains and 21 data elements, operationalizing traceability as a layered governance architecture separating enforceability-critical core elements from conditional, verification-intensive tiers. The core baseline comprises identifiers, coarse provenance, and producer-stage event records, whereas tiered mechanisms (e.g., testing and sensitive husbandry records) strengthen fraud deterrence under elevated risk. The survey results reveal broad support for traceability alongside systematic heterogeneity: data-cautious, data-aware, and data-driven profiles differ in verification-oriented priorities and digital engagement, supporting pathway-based proportional implementation.

 Originality-This study operationalizes traceability as a structured set of data elements linked to verification functions and empirically grounds a core-versus-tiered assurance model calibrated for producer heterogeneity. While empirically grounded in honey, the governance logic is transferable to other authenticity-sensitive food sectors with fragmented production, such as olive oil, spices, wine, and origin-labeled products.

title: Dynamic Complementarities in the Production of Human Capital

detail.title: Dynamic Complementarities in the Production of Human Capital
detail.abstract: Cognitive and non-cognitive skills acquired during early childhood foster later human capital investments. Heckman (2000) calls this feature dynamic complementarity (DC): skills produced at one stage raise the productivity of investment at subsequent stages. Using a census of the poor and administrative records from two social programs spanning 1994 to 2015, this paper provides empirical evidence on DC. The methodology combines an IV-RD framework to estimate the complementarity between two shocks, one early and one later in life, on secondary-school completion and standardized test performance. The early shock is attendance at Childcare Centers (CCI); the later shock is a Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) program under which poor families receive subsidies conditional on keeping their children in school. Results show that the CCT reinforces soft skills acquired in CCI, increasing secondary-school completion by about 18.3 percentage points. By contrast, receiving childcare at early stages decreases standardized test scores by 0.42 standard deviations. Although the CCT raises test scores by 0.12 standard deviations on average, it fails to offset the negative effects of the early childhood shock.

title: Economic Growth & Digital Payment Transactions in India

Digital payments have the potential to guarantee rapid economic growth. By ensuring that bank account transactions are thoroughly examined, becoming cashless will reduce the bribery system. title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Reality for Service Recovery and Customer Retention in Tourism: A Hybrid Recovery Framework
affiliations: STIE KBP and Universitas Islam Negeri Sultan Syarif Kasim Riau

detail.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Reality for Service Recovery and Customer Retention in Tourism: A Hybrid Recovery Framework
detail.abstract: Purpose: This study develops an integrated conceptual framework explaining how artificial intelligence (AI) and virtual reality (VR) technologies enhance service recovery effectiveness and customer retention in tourism and hospitality industries. This study addresses the fragmented understanding of AI and VR integration in tourism service recovery literature. Methods: A conceptual qualitative approach was employed through a systematic literature review and theory synthesis of 60 Scopus-indexed studies published between 2024 and 2026. The analysis integrates Justice Theory, Relationship Marketing Theory, Technology Acceptance Theory, and Expectation Confirmation Theory. Results: The findings indicate that AI-enabled chatbots, predictive analytics, and automated agents improve responsiveness, personalization, and recovery efficiency, while VR-based recovery experiences strengthen emotional reassurance and trust restoration. These mechanisms enhance customer satisfaction, loyalty, and retention. However, excessive automation may reduce perceived empathy and emotional authenticity, potentially weakening customer trust. The findings reveal that hybrid recovery systems combining AI efficiency and human emotional intelligence generate superior retention outcomes. Implications: The study proposes a hybrid recovery model combining AI efficiency with human emotional intelligence to optimize customer retention and sustainable competitive advantage. The framework provides theoretical insights into technology-enabled service recovery and practical guidance for tourism organizations implementing digital recovery strategies. The framework also establishes a future research agenda for AI-enabled tourism recovery ecosystems.

title: Understanding Behavioral Drivers of Neobank Adoption Among Young Consumers
affiliations: ,  and University of Delhi - Shri Ram College of Commerce

detail.title: Understanding Behavioral Drivers of Neobank Adoption Among Young Consumers
detail.abstract: Purpose The study examines factors influencing the adoption and usage of neobanking services by integrating the UTAUT2 framework with net valence theory and incorporating context-specific variables such as perceived risk, environmental consciousness, convenience and trust. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected through purposive sampling using a structured questionnaire administered to Generation Y and Z respondents. A hybrid analytical approach was adopted, combining PLS-SEM for hypothesis testing with ANN analysis. Findings Findings show that performance expectancy strongly drives behavioral intention, shaped significantly by effort expectancy and convenience, while price value also enhances intention. Social influence and hedonic motivation are not significant predictors. Trust and personal innovativeness do not moderate the relationships between perceived risk and behavioral intention or between intention and usage behavior. Environmental consciousness improves effort expectancy but not performance expectancy. Although overall perceived risk does not directly influence intention, its subdimensions meaningfully shape users' uncertainty perceptions, challenging traditional assumptions in UTAUT2. Originality/value The study integrates the UTAUT2 framework with net valence theory and incorporates context-specific variables such as perceived risk, environmental consciousness, convenience and trust, while employing a hybrid analytical approach combining PLS-SEM and ANN analysis to examine adoption and usage of neo-banking services among Generation Y and Z consumers.

title: Fame is Not Enough: Why Celebrity Status, Premium Pricing and Announcement-Only Marketing Fails in Durban Nail and Beauty SMMEs

detail.title: Fame is Not Enough: Why Celebrity Status, Premium Pricing and Announcement-Only Marketing Fails in Durban Nail and Beauty SMMEs
detail.abstract: Despite the growth of celebrity entrepreneurship in South Africa's township economy, many famous founders fail in common-service sectors. This paper examines why fame does not guarantee survival in the nail, wine, and skincare industries. Using an exploratory multiple-case study from Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, the paper presents three cases of celebrity-founded SMMEs that pursued premium pricing without differentiation and announcement-only marketing. Case 1 is a famous nail technician who charged a premium price for standard nail services in an area with many competing salons offering similar services, leading to near-closure. Case 2 is a celebrity wine brand and Case 3 is a celebrity skincare brand, both of which relied on a single announcement of their launch with no continuous marketing investment. Data was collected through direct observation, consultancy intervention, and field notes from 2024-2026. Findings show that in undifferentiated service sectors, fame provides attention but not conversion. Case 1 survived after an intervention to align pricing with market rates and invest in skill differentiation and marketing. Cases 2 and 3 failed. The paper introduces the concept of the Champion's Fallacy - the mistaken belief that past success or high profile in one domain automatically transfers to a new business without additional work. Drawing on Porter's Generic Strategies, the ResourceBased View, and Celebrity Entrepreneurship Theory, the paper argues that fame is not a VRIN resource in common services.

detail.title: Evaluating Exposure Bias in Programmatic Advertising Under Market Frictions
detail.abstract: Programmatic advertising platforms frequently optimize campaigns for cost efficiency, which can inadvertently lead to "exposure bias" by systematically excluding impressions from higher-cost demographic groups even in the absence of explicit demographic targeting. To address this challenge, we propose a multidimensional subset-scanning (MDSS) algorithm. The MDSS procedure reliably identifies the most underexposed demographic subgroups across an multidimensional feature space, enabling the bidding policy to dynamically reallocate campaign funds to marginalized subgroups. We examine the effectiveness of bias mitigation in the presence of three market frictions that advertisers frequently face: finite advertising budgets, increased competition for impressions, and information loss due to privacy restrictions. Interestingly, we find that privacy shocks (such as cookie deprecation) trigger a "misdirection effect," where obscured demographic signals in data-constrained environments can cause the algorithm to boost incorrect subgroups, thereby tricking audit metrics into registering a superficial reduction in disparity while the true exposure bias persists. We also find that competition intensifies this loss through a competitive crowding-out effect, as rivals bid away subgroup exposure. Lastly, we show that mitigating exposure bias may, counterintuitively, leave advertisers worse off with lower advertising budgets. These results yield important theoretical and managerial insights for enforcing algorithmic equity in friction-laden programmatic advertising markets.

detail.abstract: This article transforms the Hierarchy of Sustainable Marketing Strategy (HSMS) from a static typology to a dynamic, explanatory model of how firms develop and sustain sustainability strategies. We address a central gap in prior work by theorizing the mechanisms that shape progression through the hierarchy. Drawing on stakeholder, signaling, and alignment theories, we introduce two novel mechanisms to the literature. Specifically, we propose that organizational progress depends on managing: (1) the signaling gap (when external claims outpace internal change) and (2) the alignment gap (when internal structures lag strategic intent). Together, these mechanisms form an inverted U-shaped tension curve that explains why stakeholder conflicts first intensify and later subside across the hierarchy. The framework contributes to marketing theory by illuminating the temporal dynamics of sustainability tensions and to practice by offering a roadmap to anticipate motivational shifts and select appropriate strategies that align with capabilities over time.

title: Authored, Produced and Processed - Everything in Question

detail.title: Authored, Produced and Processed - Everything in Question
detail.abstract: The transparency objective behind Article 50(2) of the EU AI Act is understandable and cannot be emphasized enough. The Regulation frames this requirement as a transparency measure supporting trust and integrity and addressing risks including deception and manipulation; protecting human intellectual origin is the normative concern examined in this paper.[1][2] Readers whether individuals or institutions should be clear about machine generated content. The comment is not on transparency or to provenance technology as such. It is to the enlargement of a limited technical signal into a judgment about authorship. Participation in a production chain does not, by itself, prove origination of finished work. A transparency rule then begins to resemble a purity test. The Commission's 2026 Guidelines recognise part of this concern. Paragraph 94 clarifies that marking under Article 50(2) concerns how content was created and its artificial origin, not who created it. Yet "how created" and "who created" may remain closely connected in practical interpretation. The Guidelines state that the two are different, but do not fully define how that distinction will be preserved when a machine-readable signal is interpreted and acted upon by downstream institutions. A rule intended to protect true human creation may therefore operate as a litmus test whose decisive colour has not yet been defined, the signal identifies machine participation, but recipients may treat it as negating genuine human origination.

detail.abstract: Project context for teams using AI agents is scattered across chats, files, meeting notes, and task systems. Persistent agents retain some context, but people and agents still reconstruct it repeatedly, incurring new token costs. Agents may also confidently report stale work status as current. Existing retrieval systems, agent memory, AI-maintained knowledge files, and project briefs address parts of this problem. Some of these tools keep context in application-managed memory or databases, limiting portability. This paper asks whether a structured process using Git, Markdown, and agents can reduce recurring reconstruction costs without sacrificing accuracy while keeping work context portable across team members, agents, and runtimes. The proposed Work Registry maintains a shared Work State in Git. A scheduled agent reviews team evidence and updates source-linked work items with explicit status: open, blocked, decided, or complete. People correct those items in place; the agent preserves the corrections as evidence when regenerating the state. People and agents then use the same local files. A 570-session evaluation across two corpora and two agent runtimes compared the method with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over the raw sources. The task was to determine current work status from project histories containing stale, superseded, conflicting, or missing evidence. Because human corrections were absent from those sources, only the Registry arms could report the corrected status. Within each model, direct local-file access cost 36-59% less per query, used 15-28% fewer tokens, and achieved the highest pooled accuracy with fully valid citations. Teams with comparable workloads may see savings of this order. Evaluation materials, data, and full results: github.com/markpyzhov/work-registry-eval. AI-use disclosure: Under the author's direction, AI agents assisted in drafting and editing the text, created corpus materials, ran evaluation sessions, and produced initial scores. The author developed the method, designed the evaluation and corpora, reviewed the materials, finalized the answer keys, adjudicated scoring disagreements, and is responsible for all claims and conclusions.

title:
Procuring Sovereignty

Public Authority under the EU Cloud and AI Act

detail.title:
Procuring Sovereignty

Public Authority under the EU Cloud and AI Act
detail.abstract: The European Commission's June 2026 proposal for a Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) is the Union's most ambitious attempt to translate digital sovereignty into operative law. This article argues that the proposal is significant but structurally incomplete. CADA builds a sophisticated supply-side framework: cloud providers are classified against graduated Union assurance levels; higher levels depend on third-party assessment; contracting authorities must procure at the level indicated by risk assessment; and the proposal expressly addresses extraterritorial access, service disruption and vendor dependency. Yet the responsible public institution is constituted principally as a purchaser of qualified services, not as an administrator that must remain capable of discharging public-law duties through those services. The article develops this distinction between supplier assurance and retained operational control. It examines the proposal's cumulative legal basis under Articles 114 and 173(3) TFEU, its accommodation of Article 4(2) TEU, and its reliance on private assurance and adequacy mechanisms. It then shows why Articles 41 and 47 of the Charter expose a demand-side gap concerning reasons, evidence, correction, intervention, continuity and exit. The proposed complement is not a new constitutional settlement, but procurement and governance duties preserving non-delegable public responsibility throughout the lifecycle of digitally mediated public functions.

title: Compliance Ahead of Capacity: Institutional Isomorphism and Cybersecurity Governance Adoption in Ghana's Business Process Outsourcing and Telecommunications Sectors

detail.title: Compliance Ahead of Capacity: Institutional Isomorphism and Cybersecurity Governance Adoption in Ghana's Business Process Outsourcing and Telecommunications Sectors
detail.abstract: Ghana built formal cybersecurity governance infrastructure with unusual speed: the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038) established a licensing and accreditation regime, sectoral computer emergency response teams now span banking, telecommunications, and government, and the Bank of Ghana substantially revised its financial-sector cyber directive in 2026, its first major revision since 2018. Yet Kolog and Tijani's (2023) survey of Ghanaian financial institutions found that legal measures were by far the strongest driver of Cybersecurity Act implementation, while organisational measures, the internal governance capacity to sustain compliance, showed no significant effect at all. That finding is reported but not theoretically explained. This paper argues that institutional isomorphism (DiMaggio & Powell, 1983), together with the related concept of decoupling (Meyer & Rowan, 1977), accounts for the asymmetry: coercive pressure, exercised through statute, licensing, and audit, has outpaced the mimetic and normative pressures that typically convert formal compliance into embedded organisational capacity, leaving formal structure and operating practice loosely connected at best. Composite illustrative vignettes from Ghana's business process outsourcing and telecommunications sectors, drawn from operational experience, show the same pattern below the level of national survey data. The paper closes with implications for practitioners, who should not read legal compliance as a proxy for readiness, and an agenda for research testing the three isomorphic pressures directly against cybersecurity governance outcomes in Ghana.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates price adjustment speed and conditional volatility dynamics in the B3 Dollar futures contract following US macroeconomic announcements (Non-Farm Payroll and Consumer Price Index-CPI). Using a high-frequency dataset comprising 134,340 1-minute intraday observations from August 2025 to August 2026, we apply an intraday event study and joint ARMA(1, 0)-GARCH(1, 1)-X modeling. The findings corroborate the semi-strong form of the Efficient Market Hypothesis and highlight the rapid transmission of exogenous shocks to the Brazilian financial market microstructure.

detail.abstract: We investigate the consequences of simplifying the patient-specific geometry of an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) in flow simulations with realistic time-dependent boundary conditions. In geometrically modeled arteries, we quantify important aspects of blood flow using the realistic Apostolidis-Beris viscosity model. We solve the incompressible continuity and momentum equations on a 3D unstructured mesh using a finite-volume method. Results are presented for the original and simplified geometries in terms of 3D vortical patterns and hemodynamic indicators, including wall shear stress (WSS), time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS), oscillatory shear index (OSI), and the endothelial cell activation potential (ECAP). We demonstrate how wall shear stresses can be reliably estimated for a realistic artery using significantly faster simulations in idealized equivalent geometries. Differences in flow patterns between the original (Level 1) and the simplified (Level 2) geometries are minor, while the reduction in CPU time is substantial. However, several essential details of the flow field are lost with further simplification of the geometry (Levels 3-4), in which surface undulations are smoothed out, and the degree of asymmetry is reduced. Each simplification helps accelerate simulation while enabling prediction of the hemodynamic indicator for the original AAA artery (Level 1). The present study is a novel attempt to simplify complex arterial geometries, which enables meaningful results from the geometrically simplified equivalents.

title:
From Mobilised Savings to Delivered Financial Services: 
A Stochastic-Frontier Framework for Measuring the Institutional Conversion Gap in African Financial Systems

detail.title:
From Mobilised Savings to Delivered Financial Services: 
A Stochastic-Frontier Framework for Measuring the Institutional Conversion Gap in African Financial Systems
detail.abstract:
The rapid expansion of bank accounts, mobile money, digital payments, agent networks, deposit-taking institutions and domestic securities markets has enlarged the visible perimeter of finance in Africa. Yet the collection of savings and the multiplication of access instruments do not by themselves establish that financial systems transform available resources into services that households and firms can use. This article develops and tests a quantitative framework for measuring that missing transformation. The Institutional Conversion Gap (ICG) is defined as the distance between observed financial inclusion and a conditional potential frontier supported by mobilised savings, access infrastructure and prudential capacity. The empirical architecture distinguishes the realised outcome, represented by Block 1 (transformation, usage and allocation), from lagged structural inputs—Block 2 (savings and funding), Block 3 (access infrastructure) and Block 4 (prudential capacity)—and from conversion conditions represented by Block 5 (monetary environment) and Block 6 (fiscal environment). The structural frontier is estimated with a panel stochastic-frontier model whose production kernel is first specified as Cobb–Douglas and then tested against a constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) alternative.

The database covers 50 African countries over 2010–2024, or 750 possible country-year cells. Because no fictitious observation is introduced and incomplete lagged records are excluded, the complete estimation sample contains 464 observations from 47 countries. The selected Cobb–Douglas stochastic frontier produces an average observed-inclusion score of 26.83, an average conditional potential of 39.37, an average absolute gap of 14.82 points and average institutional conversion efficiency of 59.23 percent. Access infrastructure receives a large estimated share in the structural kernel, but this result is interpreted cautiously because Block 3 is currently built from only two sufficiently available direct annual series. Better monetary conditions are associated with a lower inefficiency scale; the fiscal coefficient is less stable and its bootstrap interval crosses zero. A CES specification yields a slightly lower Bayesian information criterion but fails the admissibility test because the optimizer does not converge and the substitution parameter reaches its upper boundary. A proposed instrument for the fiscal block is weak, the 999-replication country-cluster bootstrap converges in only 62.16 percent of replications, and the dynamic model does not outperform a last-observation benchmark in the 2022–2024 test period. The results therefore support an exploratory structural benchmark, not a validated causal ranking or superior forecasting model.

The article contributes a transparent distinction between financial presence, structural potential and realised inclusion; a reproducible mathematical chain from economic indicators to block scores, frontier potential and conversion gaps; and a governance framework for linking a multi-country econometric foundation to a subsequent country-level monitoring workbook. The findings show why savings mobilisation should be evaluated jointly with access, prudential capacity, monetary transmission and fiscal absorption, while also demonstrating that scientific validation depends as much on measurement quality, identification and stability as on a coherent theoretical model.

title: The Efficient Cross-Section is Sparse: Factor Timing and the Dimension of the SDF

detail.title: The Efficient Cross-Section is Sparse: Factor Timing and the Dimension of the SDF
detail.abstract: Out-of-sample Sharpe ratios in the cross-section of anomaly returns keep rising as principal components with negligible variance are added, an apparent violation of the near-arbitrage restriction that expected returns concentrate on a few systematic sources of risk. I argue that this pattern is a property of the payoff space empirical asset pricing studies rather than of the market it describes. Academic anomaly portfolios are held at constant weights despite predictable variation in both their premia and their risk, and are therefore unconditionally mean-variance inefficient. Applying volatility timing and mean timing to each of 212 anomalies, using only each portfolio's own return history, raises the Sharpe ratio of the large majority. In the resulting efficient cross-section, out-of-sample performance is exhausted by nine principal components, whereas the original cross-section continues to improve through 48. The discount factor built from those few components also prices the cross-section more accurately than the celebrated factor models and than its original-space counterpart, in sample and out-of-sample. Factor proliferation appears to measure unharvested timing rents rather than a large number of distinct sources of compensated risk.

detail.title: Generative AI and Mutual Fund Industry Concentration
detail.abstract: We examine whether generative artificial intelligence (GAI) changes investor search and competition in the mutual fund industry. We exploit the introduction of SearchGPT, an AI-based search interface that synthesizes real-time information and provides links to underlying sources. Following SearchGPT, the previously rising concentration of website traffic across fund families flattens, and the relative traffic advantage of large fund families declines. These effects are stronger for families that relied more heavily on traditional search and distribution channels before SearchGPT and are attenuated during GPT service outages, consistent with an AI-mediated search mechanism. The shift in investor search is also reflected in capital allocation: larger fund families lose relative shares of new sales and, more gradually, total net assets. Overall, our findings suggest that GAI can weaken search-based advantages enjoyed by large incumbents and have implications for how investor search and capital are distributed within the mutual fund industry.

title: Robust Welfare Maximization: Statistical Calibration and Full-space Policy Optimization

detail.title: Robust Welfare Maximization: Statistical Calibration and Full-space Policy Optimization
detail.abstract: We study budget-constrained treatment allocation when heterogeneous treatment benefits and costs are estimated from data. We maximize worst-case welfare subject to a worst-case budget constraint over a Wasserstein ball centered at the plug-in empirical distribution of covariates and estimated policy-evaluation scores. Our first contribution is a class-calibrated statistical analysis. Because pseudo-outcome representations are not unique, we calibrate the nominal distribution to the class of score distributions with the correct covariate marginal and conditional mean benefit and cost, rather than to a fixed oracle score distribution. If the ambiguity set intersects this policy-valid class, the robust evaluations yield simultaneous causal welfare and budget certificates. For cross-fitted augmented inverse propensity weighted scores, the Wasserstein distance to this class is bounded by an empirical-measure term plus a doubly robust product of propensity-score and outcome-or cost-regression errors. Our second contribution solves the resulting infinite-dimensional functional optimization problem. Standard Wasserstein duality theory eliminates the distributional adversary but leaves optimization over all Borel-measurable policies infinite-dimensional. We show an exact sample-wise reduction: for randomized policies, a finite-dimensional linear program followed by a Shapley extension yields a globally optimal and robustly feasible full-space policy. For deterministic policies, a mixed-integer program and nearest-neighbor extension yield explicit welfare-loss and budget-excess bounds. Simulations and a JTPA case study show favorable out-of-sample welfare and budget control.

title: People are Strange: Situated Humanness in Artificially Intelligent Contexts
affiliations: and University of Stirling

detail.title: People are Strange: Situated Humanness in Artificially Intelligent Contexts
detail.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) increasingly performs capacities historically associated with humans, the assumptions about human distinctiveness and uniqueness become increasingly unstable. We argue that existing literature largely treats humanness as a stable background reference point and therefore, overlooks how humanness itself becomes questioned and reinterpreted in AI-mediated contexts. Drawing on technological mediation theory (TTM) and the concept of defamiliarization, we develop a conceptual framework of situated humanness and its reinterpretation. We theorize humanness as a relational, contextual, and temporally dynamic experience continuously reinterpreted in relation to evolving intelligent technologies across contexts and over time. We further develop a process model explaining how AI-mediated experiences destabilize taken-for-granted understandings of humanness, render them open to reflection through defamiliarization, and initiate ongoing reinterpretation. In doing so, we reposition humanness as a central theoretical concern for understanding the future of work, human-AI interaction, and the organization of AI-mediated work itself.

detail.abstract: This paper highlights the Libyan commercial banks’ institutional environment factors, as institutional constraints on their adoption of Islamic financial transactions. Principally, in the context of formal and informal constraints, the article investigates Libyan commercial banks' external institutional environment that governs their behaviour and decisions. To achieve this end, the authors employed reports of the Libyan Central Bank, local, international reports, and the semi- structured interviews. Finally, it reviews the implications to investigate the institutional environment and the study result conducted about Libyan commercial banks. For highlighting the research gap as a future study opens up new horizons to research the effect of external environment on the commercial banks ' adoption of Islamic financial transactions. Specifically, providing a frame that includes the influence of all main actors that openly determine the commercial banks' organizational behaviour rather than only influence of bank's users.

detail.abstract: Empirical studies find Medicaid enrollment among childless adults with annual incomes well above the statutory threshold of 138 percent of the federal poverty line (FPL). Drawing on federal Medicaid regulations and CMS guidance on MAGI household and income-verification requirements, this paper shows that the discrepancy can arise from using annual income to approximate monthly eligibility and from differences in household-income construction. Using monthly data from the 2013-2016 Survey of Income and Program Participation, we construct a lowest-monthly-earnings (LME) measure and show that Medicaid enrollment declines by 5.7 percentage points at the eligibility threshold among childless adults. Applying these insights to the Current Population Survey over the same period, we construct an annual-data eligibility measure that identifies a 6-9 percentage-point decline in Medicaid enrollment across a range of specifications. Finally, we characterize the relationship between LME and annual income, showing how monthly eligibility can correspond to annual incomes above 138 percent of the FPL and thereby reconcile statutory eligibility rules with enrollment patterns documented in prior studies.

title: Rolling the Dice: A Practitioner's Framework for Call Center Platform Migration in Technology M&A

detail.title: Rolling the Dice: A Practitioner's Framework for Call Center Platform Migration in Technology M&A
detail.abstract: A call center is the one part of a technology merger where the customer is on the line while the integration is happening. This paper closes out a three-part practitioner series on technology M&A: it applies the general integration sequencing proposed in prior work, and the agentic schema-convergence architecture proposed in companion research, specifically to contact center platform migration-arguably the highest-stakes, most real-time-constrained system in the entire technology integration scope. The paper works through the full sequence as practiced: architectural discovery of both the source and destination contact center platforms; a lift-and-shift versus new-platform-build decision framework; combined schema design across five distinct artifact types-tickets, image/attachment queues, forms, letters, and reports-deliberately favoring an inclusive superset design over a from-scratch canonical rebuild, because historical ticket fidelity across both merging companies is a hard requirement, not a nicety; a staged NPE → UAT → Production data migration pipeline run in parallel with new-platform feature development; a stakeholder-gated MVP definition requiring full dual-system functional parity; data-steward certification criteria specific to each artifact type; a pre-go-live validation stage where the existing agent workforce tests production-like data on the new platform before cutover; and an extension of the five-agent AASC architecture with two contact-center-specific agents. Real-world adoption data on contact center AI and CCaaS integration challenges is used throughout to ground the framework's claims. Unlike the two earlier papers in this series, which were written ahead of field validation, this paper is grounded directly in what worked in practice on an actual technology M&A call center migration-the sequencing, the schema approach, and the certification gates described here reflect real implementation experience, not a pre-execution proposal.

detail.abstract: We show that optimal execution under nonlinear transient market impact can be represented as a transformer sequence model. The propagator becomes causal attention; the execution strategy's cost becomes the forward pass through a neural network. This opens up the possibility of using a neural-network-optimized stack, such as PyTorch and the Adam optimizer on Nvidia GPUs, to compute optimal trading paths in the propagator model, as well as to train model parameters from realized executions of metaorders. For power-law impact and decay, our method matches or improves on the table of optimal values reported by Curato, Gatheral, and Lillo (2017), and on signed schedules reaches those values significantly faster than the sequential quadratic programming method. A single batched descent allows us to map signed-acquisition costs together with round-trip manipulation certificates across a plane parameterized by the impact and propagator exponents. A similar batched computation locates the slippage frontier at a manipulable exponent pair, where slippage renders the signed execution problem well posed.

title: Has Your Company Gone Quiet, or Just Given Up?
affiliations: , American University of Sharjah, University of New Mexico - Robert O. Anderson Schools of Management, Universidad de los Andes, Colombia and University of Oslo

detail.title: Has Your Company Gone Quiet, or Just Given Up?
detail.abstract:
Under massive political and geopolitical pressures, companies are quietly stripping the visibility from their social activities. A survey of 400 CSR and ESG executives in both Europe and the USA shows why this silence matters, and what it costs companies now and in the future.

Idea in Brief
The finding. A survey of 400 senior executives at large US and European firms operating in high-risk and crisis-affected markets finds the corporate social and environmental agenda intact, but driven underground. Firms are conserving the substance of their commitments while spending down their visibility, mostly under pressure from their own governments.

The risk. Going quiet may be strategic but it carries long-term costs. Stakeholders cannot distinguish between quiet commitment and quiet retreat, while public visibility no longer reinforces internal accountability. Over time, this low-visibility environment can encourage commitments to gradually and quietly erode.

The response. Managers should preserve social substance even when its visibility declines, but also build organizational capabilities for incorporating home-government pressures into risk assessments, capture and scale crisis management know-how, and bring younger employees into frontline decision-making as sensors for emerging social and political risks.

title: Digital Transformation of R&D Project Management in Knowledge-Intensive Organizations: A Conceptual Framework
affiliations: MGIMO University

detail.title: Digital Transformation of R&D Project Management in Knowledge-Intensive Organizations: A Conceptual Framework
detail.abstract: The accelerating pace of technological change has made digital transformation a central concern for organizations managing complex, knowledgeintensive research and development (R&D) projects. This paper synthesizes findings from the author's master's research to propose a conceptual framework for the digital transformation of R&D project management in technology-intensive organizations. Drawing on a systematic review of academic literature and comparative analysis of digital tool adoption across sectors, the paper identifies three core technological pillarsintegrated data platforms, Internet of Things (IoT) sensing, and digital twin modellingand examines the organizational, financial, and human-capital barriers that constrain their effective deployment. The proposed framework conceptualizes digital transformation as an iterative managerial cycle spanning strategic goal-setting, cross-functional integration, real-time monitoring, and institutional knowledge capture, rather than as a one-time technology procurement exercise. The paper argues that sustainable digital maturity in R&D-intensive organizations depends on aligning technology adoption with organizational design, regulatory compliance, and long-term knowledge management practices.

title: Work-related Learning and Professional Growth of Students at a Selected Open University in Zimbabwe
affiliations: Durban University of Technology (DUT),  and Durban University of Technology

detail.title: Work-related Learning and Professional Growth of Students at a Selected Open University in Zimbabwe
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between work-related learning (WRL) and the professional development of students at Zimbabwe Open University. The purpose of the research, guided by Experiential Learning Theory, is to identify how WRL influences students' employability, problemsolving abilities, and entrepreneurial skills. Using a quantitative approach, data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 148 third-year Commerce students. The data were analyzed using both descriptive and inferential statistical methods. Findings suggest that WRL significantly improves students' problem-solving skills and employability. Conversely, a notable negative correlation was observed between WRL and the development of entrepreneurial skills, indicating that structured workplace environments may limit creativity. Students also reported facing challenges related to mentorship and the alignment between academic learning and industry expectations. The study concludes that while WRL is essential for preparing students for the workforce, its design should be optimized to support more comprehensive professional development. It is recommended that universities and industry partners strengthen collaboration by integrating structured mentorship programs, aligning curricula more closely with industry requirements, and intentionally promoting entrepreneurial skill development within WRL initiatives.

detail.abstract: Springer Nature currently lists Ivan Oransky as an Editorial Board member of Research Integrity and Peer Review, with affiliations to the Center for Scientific Integrity (CSI) and New York University. CSI identifies him as its Executive Director and as co-founder of Retraction Watch, while Retraction Watch describes its work as reporting on retractions and related research-integrity events and maintains a database integrated into Crossref infrastructure. The journal's scope expressly covers competing interests, misconduct by authors, reviewers and editors, editorial decision-making and post-publication review. This is therefore not an incidental overlap between unrelated professional activities. It is a same-domain role convergence. The public record does not show that Oransky handled any manuscript, influenced any editorial decision, sought any particular retraction, disclosed an inadequate interest, or received payment tied to a case. Those allegations are not made. The governance problem is narrower and stronger: Springer Nature's public materials do not identify why he was selected, what his actual responsibilities are, whether recurrent Retraction Watch/CSI intersections are screened as non-financial competing interests, or whether recusals are recorded and auditable. Springer Nature and BMC policies require editorial-board members to declare competing interests and exclude themselves from affected manuscripts. Where the journal studies the same institutions, editorial actions and integrity actors covered by the appointee's organisation, a generic policy is not enough. The appointment should not be treated as neutral institutional validation unless Springer Nature publishes a role description, a case-screening rule, a confidentiality firewall and a meaningful recusal mechanism. If recurrent conflicts make those safeguards impracticable, role separation is the more defensible default.

China is fully committed to industrial and technology policy. The policy motives of security and self-reliance received even greater emphasis as the US-China trade war reached its peak between April and October 2025, and a major mobilization of resources is being sustained. New policy instruments and new forms of direct government intervention have been rolled out steadily in recent months. The number of industrial sectors designated for policy support remains exceptionally high. These features define a new phenomenon I label China Industrial Policy 3.0 (China IP 3.0). The costs of this substantial industrial policy effort are likely high, particularly when we include the indirect macroeconomic and institutional costs along with direct costs. However, China shows no sign of wavering from its commitment to technological competition with the United States, and if anything, we may observe China doubling down as we enter 2026.
