detail.title: Stablecoins Meet the Mundell-Fleming Trilemma

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of New York Staff Report No. 1202
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study how stablecoins impact global capital flows by constructing a novel wallet-level dataset linking geotagged Ethereum Name Service registrations to stablecoin transactions around banking restrictions, currency crises, sanctions, and monetary disruptions. We find that crisis-country wallets experience significant increases in USD stablecoin inflows and receipt activity during crisis weeks. Motivated by this evidence, we develop a small-open-economy New Keynesian model in which household adoption of programmable stablecoins weakens the government's enforcement technology for capital controls by making capital mobility endogenous. The empirical evidence validates the model's central assumption that flight pressure increases stablecoin adoption. Stablecoins therefore tighten the Mundell-Fleming trilemma by reducing the government's ability to sustain independent monetary policy under a fixed exchange-rate regime.

title: Minimum Effort, Maximum Efficiency: The Evolution of IJF Judo from 2009-2026

detail.title: Minimum Effort, Maximum Efficiency: The Evolution of IJF Judo from 2009-2026
detail.abstract: We assemble the population record of International Judo Federation competition-221,875 contests across seven rule regimes (2009-2026), with 328,346 athlete-attributed within-fight events-to ask what rule changes actually change. Auditing the regimes against primary rule texts and holding measurement to a fixed competitive tier, we find a pair of invariances flanking the margins policy moves. Rules reallocate scoring production dramatically between standing and ground judo, yet the technique hierarchy within each phase never reorders; each technique carries a stable conversion signature that reforms re-price but do not re-rank. A by-production technology with distinct standing (tachiwaza) and ground (newaza) goods relations and costly disposable penalty generation models the athlete level, with union meta-frontier inference via smoothed bootstrap extending the pattern to production: the ground game's share of athlete inefficiency (∼56%) is statistically indistinguishable across regimes, standing technology gaps close monotonically toward the present, and the penalty and concession-generating technologies are era-invariant. These conclusions survive re estimation on sex-specific frontiers, which additionally reveal a symmetric division of the pooled technology: men anchor the standing frontier, women the groundwork frontier. Sex-specific frontiers preserve every ordering while revealing a symmetric division of the pooled frontier: men anchor the standing technology, women the groundwork. Convexifying the meta-frontier across regimes would manufacture a quarter to half of the measured gaps from blends of rulebooks that never existed. The most recent liberalization lowered the mean penalty rate while raising its estimated feasible floor removing the offense athletes could avoid while enlarging the one they cannot. Rule reform, on this evidence, redraws the price system athletes face far more readily than it changes what athletes are able to do.

detail.abstract: Government transfers vary along two design dimensions that standard models predict should not matter: whether benefits are paid in cash or kind, and whether they arrive as one-time or recurring payments. We test to what extent these design choices a!ect household spending using sharp changes in four pandemic-era transfers to lowincome families with children: one-time food vouchers, monthly food benefits, one-time cash payments, and monthly cash payments. Linking variation in benefit timing and amount to high-frequency household scanner data, we estimate spending responses in a harmonized di!erence-in-di!erences and event-study framework. We find that households spend more out of in-kind benefits than out of cash transfers of similar value, and more out of recurring payments than out of one-time transfers in the short-run. Our estimates produce the first internally comparable set of shortrun food-store MPCs across di!erent transfer types ranging from 0.18 (one-time) and 0.38 (monthly) for in-kind benefits, versus 0.06 (one-time) and 0.20 (monthly) for cash. The patterns suggest that the form and timing of transfers systematically shape household spending in ways that are consistent with mental accounting, labeling, and forward-looking responses. More broadly, our results imply that transfer design-not just generosity and targeting-is a first-order policy lever for both social insurance and short-run demand stabilization.

title: Street Spin Foam: A Preliminary Formulation

detail.title: Street Spin Foam: A Preliminary Formulation
detail.abstract: Movement through a city is usually modelled by fixing a geometry, placing agents inside it, and treating the worth of a location as a number attached to that location. This paper develops a representation in which relations carry the state instead. A street district is written as a compact lattice gauge theory of valuation on a two-complex, in the spin-foam representation of covariant loop quantum gravity. Persons, places and stores become onecells, that is, worldlines, and the two-cells become the histories of the relations among them, so that being somewhere is a relation with a history rather than a coordinate a person carries. An entity is then a constraint on how the relations meeting at it may combine, rather than a bearer of state. Two consequences follow. Supplying a group and an action makes the spins, the intertwiners and the vertex amplitude follow from a character expansion rather than from stipulation, so that a large collection of local weights reduces to a small number of global choices; the expansion is verified against an independent numerical evaluation. Pedestrians then enter as charged matter, minimally coupled, and Kolmogorov's criterion yields a prediction sharper than the statement that valuation affects movement: circulation is sourced by the topological part of the valuation field alone, so that a region of large local disagreement and zero winding carries zero net circulation. A model whose forces are gradients of potentials leaves that pattern inaccessible, which makes the difference testable rather than interpretive. A case study on the street network of Ginza, Tokyo, with constructed commercial content, illustrates what the formalism does. The gauge structure changes simulated behaviour against a flat-connection control; circulation tracks the winding number while leaving a matched non-topological predictor inert; an effective distance read off correlation decay departs from street distance; encounter order is inert under an abelian connection and becomes material as soon as the valuation axes separate; and a walk on the complex sees an effective two-dimensional geometry over about a decade and a half of scale. One prediction fails, and its diagnosis is the most transferable result: it was imported from a confining gauge theory that the model leaves uninstantiated. The cell assignment admits two orientations, with entities on edges or objects on faces, and a counting argument bears on which of them leaves a configuration space to sample. Under the second, persons enter the spin foam directly, on condition that the one-cells are occasions gathering several parties rather than pairwise relations. The contribution is a representation in which relations rather than sites carry the state, a route by which local weights follow from a group and an action, a falsifiable point of difference from gradient-based models, and a criterion for choosing the cell assignment. Estimating the couplings from observation is identified as the next stage.

title: The Scope of Situated Judgment: An Ontology of the Judged Subject in a Generative Relational Framework

detail.title: The Scope of Situated Judgment: An Ontology of the Judged Subject in a Generative Relational Framework
detail.abstract: Judgments of persons are routinely formed inside one relation and used inside another. A supervisor's account of a researcher is read by an admissions committee; a clinician's formulation follows a patient into a dierent service; an electorate that has never met a candidate decides on the strength of endorsements by those who claim to know him. This paper asks what such a judgment warrants once it leaves the relation in which it was formed. On the framework used here, what a relation generates is generated within it and is available only from the positions its parties occupied, so an attribute exhibited in one relation is not thereby a property carried into others. The paper distinguishes two claims about assessment that are usually run together: that a judgment is a noisy estimate of a real underlying quality, for which the remedies are structure and de-biasing, and that there is no such quality to estimate, for which those remedies are misdirected. It argues that both hold, in dierent domains, and states where the boundary falls. A limiting case is then examined in which a referee signs an account written by its subject: no shared experience exists and the instrument functions regardless, which indicates that such instruments do not carry an account of a relation at all. What they transmit is a eld of relational conditions that recongures what the person can subsequently generate; the account is the justication oered for opening that eld rather than the thing conveyed. This explains why an empty instrument works, why such instruments are exchanged for things other than accounts, and why the same property that lets an unassessable person enter a system is what makes the instrument tradeable. Two cases are compared, political selection and academic recommendation, and the comparison is drawn not through the motives of those who judge but through the regime under which judgments are issued: who may issue one, at what weight, with what observational access, with what transferability, and under what provision for revision. The paper's positive proposal follows from the political case. Political theory did not resolve the problem of judging a candidate by making judgment more accurate; it made the mandate revisable. That remedy is institutional and temporal rather than epistemic, and it generalises. Where the paper's claims are already made by professional assessment standards, by the conferralist account of social properties, or by the selection model of representation, they are conceded rather than asserted.

title: Education as a Nutritional Redistributor: Income, Diet Quality, and the Demand for Nutrients in Brazil
affiliations: CAEN - UFC

detail.title: Education as a Nutritional Redistributor: Income, Diet Quality, and the Demand for Nutrients in Brazil
detail.abstract: We estimate a Quadratic Almost Ideal Demand System (QUAIDS) for twelve food groups plus tobacco and alcohol-included to capture substitution with addictive goods-using microdata from Brazil's 2017-18 Household Budget Survey, correcting sample-selection bias via bivariate copulas selected empirically by canonical maximum likelihood estimation. We propose a method to derive nutritional income elasticities from a nutritional content matrix-a mapping from food-group demand to nutrient demand that extends any estimated demand system to produce nutritional elasticities without requiring a separate nutrient equation system. With this structure, we specify education-income interaction effects that reveal a pattern consistent with the redistribution-rather than a uniform increase-of nutritional sensitivity to income. Protein is the only nutrient with an income elasticity above unity, while protective micronutrients-vitamin C, fiber, calcium-respond significantly less to income. The main result lies in education: the education gradient is asymmetric-tertiary-educated households exhibit lower income elasticities for protein and zinc, but higher elasticities for 1 vitamin C, fiber, and calcium-so that the same income increment is associated with distinct nutritional returns depending on household education. This asymmetry suggests that the nutritional effectiveness of income transfer programs such as Bolsa Família varies with the educational level of the beneficiary household-a pattern that points to a possible complementarity between income and education in such policies.

detail.abstract: For eighty-one years no state has used a nuclear weapon in war. This article asks what would follow if that record were broken not in a great-power exchange but in a counter-proliferation strike against a non-nuclear-weapon state — specifically, against hardened nuclear infrastructure in Iran. It develops three findings. The discrimination paradox: over a specified range, normative damage varies inversely with humanitarian magnitude, because norm reinforcement requires a moral repertoire that a discriminate strike does not supply. The relationship is non-monotonic, peaking at the minimum casualty level consistent with demonstrated utility, which locates the maximally corrosive variant at the hard-target strike rather than at a zero-casualty demonstration. Reclassification: the likely outcome is neither the norm’s death nor its renewal but its amendment into conditional permission, through a four-move sequence each step of which is observable. Institutional displacement: the load-bearing casualty is the safeguards system rather than the Security Council. Using the 2025–26 conventional campaigns as a within-case baseline, the article isolates the nuclear variable’s marginal contribution and states a falsification test against currently reported data. A two-by-two crossing perceived success against discrimination yields the central finding: the modal outcome in actual terms is the least corrosive cell and in perceived terms the most corrosive, and that divergence — sustained by verification collapse — is where the danger lies.

title: The Wider Effects of Higher Pension Ages: Evidence on Labor Supply, Welfare Spillovers, and Savings

detail.title: The Wider Effects of Higher Pension Ages: Evidence on Labor Supply, Welfare Spillovers, and Savings
detail.abstract: We study the effects of a six-month increase in Denmark's early, incentivized, and full pension ages using a regression discontinuity design. Over 12 years, we estimate responses in employment, benefit claiming, and savings. The reform increased the average retirement age by 3.3 months, driven by strong labor-supply responses during newly restricted eligibility periods and persistent effects thereafter. Extended employment is accompanied by higher savings, with no evidence of anticipatory adjustment. Responses around early eligibility ages align with financial incentives, whereas those near the full pension age appear norm-driven. Strong labor-supply responses and limited spillovers into alternative benefits generate fiscal gains.

title: Multiple Reference and the Reconstruction of Co-Experience: A Generative Relational Account of Recommendation Procedure

detail.title: Multiple Reference and the Reconstruction of Co-Experience: A Generative Relational Account of Recommendation Procedure
detail.abstract: Institutions that select people by reference almost always ask for more than one. This paper takes that requirement seriously and asks what it is for. On the account developed here, the shared experience between a candidate and a referee is not an object that either party holds and one of them writes down. It is generated within their relation, and each account of it is a projection taken from one relational position. Asking for several references is therefore an attempt to reconstruct an object from its presentations, in the way that what identies an attractor is what remains invariant across trajectories. The institution is doing something structurally correct and doing it badly. Four consequences follow for the design of the procedure. What matters among sources is independence of relational position rather than the number of letters. What carries information is what survives across projections rather than their average or their maximum. Symbolic authority accrues to those whose time is scarce, so an eminent referee supplies a thin projection, and weighting by authority is accordingly the least suitable weighting for a reconstruction. And the calibration of individual referees, which no institution maintains, is a precondition for correcting the distortion each introduces. Two failures of procedure are then identied: evaluators collapse onto the single most authoritative account, which discards the reconstruction and returns the decision to one projection; and the candidate, who is one of the two producers of the experience, contributes no account at all. The paper proposes that the candidate's structured account be collected as a required source at the time references are requested. It closes with the injustice that survives every correction it proposes, including a paradox in which contesting an account may destroy the relation that generated the standing to contest it. The paper's central empirical premise, that divergence among sources carries information, is contested in the literature it draws on, and the paper argues for it rather than assuming it.

detail.title: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Maximal Extractable Value Allocation under Proposer-Builder Separation

detail.abstract: We develop a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for analyzing Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) allocation in decentralized exchange (DEX) markets under Proposer-Builder Separation (PBS). The model follows the PBS block-production pipeline from uninformed DEX-user transactions to searcher bundle construction, builder block assembly, proposer block selection, and on-chain execution. Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MARL) optimizes participant policies in this shared execution environment, and average approximate best-response (ABR) regret quantifies the residual unilateral gains found by a finite evaluation procedure that holds all other agents' policies fixed and retrains one agent at a time. In a two-pool, single-token-pair experimental instantiation, we compare a configuration with two back-running searchers against a mixed configuration with one sandwich searcher and one back-running searcher. This distinction matters because a back-running transaction is appended after observed order flow and does not change the amount of output tokens received by the original uninformed trader, whereas a sandwich attack places searcher transactions around a targeted victim swap and can reduce the amount of output tokens received by that trader. The results show that MEV-related cumulative rewards are allocated differently across these configurations. Searchers convert visible order flow into bundle profits, builders aggregate these bundles through block construction, and builder competition transfers part of the resulting value to the proposer through block bids. Permitting sandwich attacks lowers uninformed traders' cumulative rewards and increases reward asymmetry among searchers.

title: Space-Based Data Providers in the EU and U.S.

detail.title: Space-Based Data Providers in the EU and U.S.
detail.abstract: Can the EU Space Act streamline European space licensing without imposing broad new compliance burdens on firms outside Europe? This paper examines the March 2026 Compromise Text and its legal context to answer this question. In this version of the Act, the term "space-based data provider" maps onto no established EU legal category and has a circular definition. The result may not be a full-fledged data regime so much as regulatory uncertainty for foreign firms with respect to proportionality, anticircumvention, and the third-country equivalence provisions applied to regimes such as that of the United States. Uncertainty itself can be a compliance burden and may undercut the streamlining the legislation is meant to deliver. Because the U.S. has no single space regulator capable of granting the reciprocal recognition that the statute demands, a sector-specific agreement may be the only realistic pathway to fulfill this goal. The paper also addresses changes made between the June 2025 draft proposal which treated the cyber provisions as lex specialis, a sector-specific override of the NIS2 Directive, while the March 2026 Compromise Text reversed course and yields without prejudice to the NIS2 regime.

title: The Temporal Fit Evaluation Framework (TFEF): Selecting Evaluation Methods in AI-Native Projects

detail.abstract: AI-native projects need evaluation, but the methods available for it are not interchangeable across a project's timeline. House's (1980) eight established evaluation approaches, as elaborated for health informatics by Friedman and Wyatt (2006) and summarized for public health AI by Wu (2026), differ in when they can be used: some set their criteria before an outcome exists, others require a system already running in real-world use. This paper proposes the Temporal Fit Evaluation Framework (TFEF), defined by exactly that property-whether a method's criteria can be set before an outcome exists or only once one does-and makes two contributions. First, TFEF sorts House's eight methods by temporal fit: four apply directly to the upfront stage of an AI-native project, before deployment; two contribute as upfront elicitation input; three require the system to be live. Second, it turns that classification into practice-a criteria-based guide for selecting which upfront method, or combination, fits a given project, and a brief illustrative case showing the guide redirect an agentic workflow's design before any code is written, not merely validate a design already chosen. This is a conceptual contribution, not an empirical one: its claims rest on definitional and logical grounds, not new data. We close by noting two further uses of the same upfront artifacts-supporting AI governance review, and, in agentic systems, becoming part of the agent's own operating context.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing how citizenship is exercised. Decisions about welfare, mobility, work, knowledge and political communication increasingly depend on data and automated systems operating across territorial and legal boundaries. These systems also require energy, water, minerals, labour and land, revealing the physical limits of seemingly immaterial digitalisation. Established accounts of digital citizenship explain rights, participation, inclusion and people's capacity to act through data. They give less attention, however, to ecological costs, ownership of essential infrastructure and consequences that extend across places and generations. This chapter develops EcoTechnoPolitical Citizenship as a framework connecting these concerns. It defines citizenship as the practical capacity to claim digital rights, participate in collective decisions, shape technological infrastructure and accept ecological responsibilities according to each actor's power and contribution. The framework has four dimensions: the physical and ecological basis of digital systems; democratic control over infrastructure; meaningful citizen agency; and responsibility across territories, supply chains and generations. The chapter traces the development of digital citizenship towards automated public life and explains AI economics through data, computing capacity, finance, labour and public dependence. It then examines the digital-green transition, which seeks to align digitalisation with sustainability but often leaves technological growth outside enforceable ecological limits. Practical implications are developed for impact assessment, public digital infrastructure, data commons, territorial oversight, citizen participation and education. Particular attention is paid to unequal power among citizens, governments, firms and communities affected by infrastructure. EcoTechnoPolitical Citizenship ultimately provides an accessible conceptual map for governing AI-dependent societies democratically while respecting planetary limits.

title: An empirical study of the stress factors affecting the mental health of Australian construction workers
affiliations: University of New South Wales (UNSW) - University of New South Wales School of Built Environment, University of New South Wales (UNSW) and University of New South Wales (UNSW)

detail.title: An empirical study of the stress factors affecting the mental health of Australian construction workers
detail.abstract: The Australian construction industry records a markedly elevated suicide rate, yet the evidence on its drivers has been predominantly subjective, cross-sectional and descriptive. Drawing on administrative data for the six Australian states and two territories over 2001–2021 (N = 168), this study constructs entropy-weighted TOPSIS indices of three demand-side stressors—work-related, employment and financial stress—and links them to the construction-worker suicide rate within a panel framework. Conditional associations are estimated by two-way fixed effects and tested for robustness; endogeneity is addressed by instrumental-variable estimation using four resource-side constructs, supported by weak-instrument diagnostics, weak-instrument-robust inference and exclusion-restriction sensitivity analysis; functional-form assumptions are relaxed through an instrumental-variable double machine-learning estimator with support-vector nuisance functions (IV-DML-SVM); and the stressors are ranked by Shapley variance decomposition and permutation importance with formal tests of statistical distinguishability. Work-related stress is the foremost and most robust driver: dominated by occupational heat exposure, which a placebo test shows it is specific to construction, and ranked first on every importance criterion applied. Employment and financial stress are positive but secondary, sensitive to specification and mutually indistinguishable, with no stable order between them. The findings convert long-standing impressions about the rank order of construction-industry stressors into triangulated, policy-relevant evidence.

title: Forecast, Decision, and Order as Separate Objects: A Contract-Based Evaluation Architecture for Multi-Agent Market Systems

detail.title: Forecast, Decision, and Order as Separate Objects: A Contract-Based Evaluation Architecture for Multi-Agent Market Systems
detail.abstract: Multi-agent market systems often collapse prediction, action selection, and execution into a single agent output, obscuring the provenance and independent evaluation of errors. This study evaluates a contract-based architecture in which Forecast, Decision, and Order are distinct objects with separate lifecycles and evidence boundaries. Forecasts are immutable probability-bearing objects bound to explicit targets, horizons, data cutoffs, strategy/model identifiers, and replay evidence; decision utility and execution are evaluated downstream. The empirical study uses a frozen historical replay. The primary experiment contains hourly BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, and SOLUSDT data from 2024-2025 with a six-hour event target and a 2025H2 out-of-sample test. Relative to equalweight raw aggregation, calibrated weighting reduced Brier loss by 0.01639 for BTC, 0.01357 for ETH, and 0.01208 for SOL; paired 24-hour moving-block bootstrap 95% intervals were entirely below zero for all three comparisons. Additional ablations did not support general superiority for correlation penalties, disagreement shrinkage, regimespecific weighting, shadow cold-start, or a volatility-based decision veto; these negative findings are retained. An independent daily replication on SPY, QQQ, and GLD produced calibration-improvement point estimates in the same direction, but all 95% moving-block bootstrap intervals crossed zero. The evidence supports explicit probabilistic calibration and receipt-backed forecast evaluation in the frozen replay. It does not support claims of trading profitability, production readiness, universal cross-market superiority, causal superiority of the architecture, or autonomous market intelligence.

title: The Long-Lasting Effects of Bombing on Environmental Management. Evidence from Kosovo
affiliations: University of Reading

detail.title: The Long-Lasting Effects of Bombing on Environmental Management. Evidence from Kosovo
detail.abstract: This paper studies how wartime destruction shapes the quality of post-conflict reconstruction and local state capacity, focusing on waste management infrastructure in Kosovo. Exploiting plausibly exogenous variation in NATO bombing intensity during the 1999 conflict and the staggered construction of post-war waste landfills, I estimate difference-in-differences and triple-difference models comparing births at varying distances from landfill sites. The results show that children born within 6 km of landfills in heavily bombed municipalities are 3.3–4.6 percentage points more likely to die before their first birthday (approximately 33–46 additional deaths per 1,000 births), corresponding to a 118–164 percent increase relative to the baseline infant mortality rate of 28 per 1,000. Consistent with weakened local oversight and governance capacity, heavily bombed municipalities that host landfills exhibit higher perceived corruption in local government. Together, these findings indicate that conflict-induced institutional degradation can compromise post-conflict infrastructure provision, generating persistent and severe health costs. The paper highlights the political economy of reconstruction as a key channel through which war imposes long-run welfare losses.

title: The Pre-BOJ Announcement Drift: Evidence from Japanese Equity Indices

detail.title: The Pre-BOJ Announcement Drift: Evidence from Japanese Equity Indices
detail.abstract: We document a large and robust pre-announcement drift in Japanese equity indices ahead of scheduled Bank of Japan (BOJ) monetary policy decisions: prices drift up steadily in the days before a meeting, peak immediately ahead of the decision, and do not continue afterward, earning an economically large and statistically significant excess return without elevated volatility. The drift is concentrated in meetings preceded by high ex-ante implied volatility. It is the Bank-of-Japan analog of the pre-FOMC drift of Lucca and Moench (2015), with a distinctive Japanese feature-variable announcement timing-that aids identification.

title: Non-economic Attributes and Marriage Matching: An Analysis of China's Hukou Inheritance Reform
affiliations: Zhejiang University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - Department of Economics, Jinan University and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Non-economic Attributes and Marriage Matching: An Analysis of China's Hukou Inheritance Reform
detail.abstract: This paper studies how institutional status shapes marital matching under China's hukou system. We exploit a reform allowing children to inherit hukou status from either parent rather than only their mother. Using census data and a triple-difference design, we find that the reform increased rural women's likelihood of marrying an urban-local man by 7.4 percentage points relative to urban women. These effects were stronger in cities with greater availability of urban-local men. To quantify the reform's contribution to marriage distribution, we estimate the Choo and Siow (2006) structural model to conduct counterfactual analyses. Changes in marital gains account for substantial shares of the 1995-2005 changes in marriage rates and hukoubased matching patterns. The reform accounts for 1.79 points (22%) of the decline in rural-local women's marriage rate and 3.51 points (64%) of the rise in rural-nonlocal matching. Overall, the reform reallocated marriage opportunities from locals to nonlocals.

title: Scaling Tokenized Markets under Sponsor Governance
affiliations: University of Calgary - Haskayne School of Business, Korea Capital Market Institute (KCMI) and Department of Fintech, SKK Business School, Sungkyunkwan University

detail.title: Scaling Tokenized Markets under Sponsor Governance
detail.abstract: A central policy question for tokenized markets is whether efforts to promote adoption are matched by the organizational capabilities needed to keep shared services operating. Tokenization can improve certification and market depth, yet growth can strain custody, servicing, settlement, and liquidity capacity. We develop a model in which internal resources and precommitted facilities absorb stress before remaining need reaches a sponsor. The sponsor supplies missing resources only when continued operation is worth the cost. At the margin, resilience improves as adoption expands only when the sponsor's credible support limit keeps pace with the residual burden created by scale. Otherwise, network effects can coexist with a fragile high-adoption outcome. For a given adoption level, sponsor support rises with need up to that limit and disappears beyond it, so the largest requests may receive no support. Portability limits losses after withdrawal. When it leaves the sponsor's continuation incentive unchanged, private investment can be too low if platforms capture only part of users' continuity benefit. No general ranking follows when portability weakens the sponsor's incentive to continue. In the bank application, intermediate stress can shift losses to depositors before larger shocks induce withdrawal. The framework identifies policy targets and trade-offs rather than a single optimal instrument mix. It suggests assessing subsidies, sandboxes, and common standards together with internal capacity, ring-fenced resources, recovery arrangements, clear limits on sponsor support, and portable core services.

title: Does QDMTT Neutralize Section 10AA? A Simulation of Pillar Two, India SEZ and Belgium Holding

detail.title: Does QDMTT Neutralize Section 10AA? A Simulation of Pillar Two, India SEZ and Belgium Holding

detail.abstract: The OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework's Pillar Two rules impose a 15% global minimum effective tax rate (ETR) on large multinational enterprise (MNE) groups. A central open question for practitioners and policymakers is whether income-based tax incentives-such as India's Special Economic Zone (SEZ) profit-linked deduction under Section 10AA of the Income-tax Act-retain any economic value once a host or intermediary jurisdiction introduces a Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (QDMTT). This paper develops an illustrative, transaction-level simulation of a stylised US-parented, Belgium-holding, Indiaoperating MNE structure to quantify how a prospective Indian QDMTT would interact with the Substance-Based Income Exclusion (SBIE) and with Belgium's own minimum-tax exposure. As of Union Budget 2025-26 (February 2025), India had not legislated a QDMTT, IIR or UTPR (EY India, 2024); the analysis is therefore explicitly forward-looking rather than a description of enacted law. The simulation suggests that a fully income-based incentive such as Section 10AA would retain only 10-15% of its nominal value under a prospective QDMTT once excess profit is taxed up to 15%, while the SBIE preserves a smaller, substance-linked benefit. The paper closes with a research design for a difference-indifferences extension using Prowess and Orbis firm-level data, intended as the empirical core of a doctoral dissertation.

title: Climate-Resilient Retail Lending: A Framework for Integrating Climate Risk, Sustainable Banking, and Financial Innovation

detail.title: Climate-Resilient Retail Lending: A Framework for Integrating Climate Risk, Sustainable Banking, and Financial Innovation
detail.abstract:
Climate-related financial risks are becoming increasingly material to banking institutions, with growing evidence suggesting that physical climate hazards and transition-related economic adjustments can influence borrower resilience, collateral quality, and mortgage lending outcomes. While substantial progress has been made in climate-risk measurement, sustainable finance, and banking regulation, comparatively limited attention has been devoted to understanding how climate-risk insights can be translated into retail lending practices and lending-product design.

This study addresses this gap by investigating the relationship between climate-related risks and mortgage lending outcomes and by examining how climate-risk information can be systematically incorporated into retail lending practices to enhance banking resilience while supporting climate adaptation and the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy. The research develops a climate-resilient retail lending framework that links climate-risk exposure, mortgage lending outcomes, and climate-responsive lending design.

The study adopts a sequential mixed-methods approach combining theoretical synthesis, quantitative analysis, and expert validation. The empirical component focuses on the U.S. mortgage market and utilizes publicly available mortgage, banking, climate, and socioeconomic datasets to examine whether climate-risk indicators provide explanatory value beyond conventional credit-risk determinants. Findings are subsequently translated into framework development and refined through engagement with banking practitioners, credit-risk specialists, climate-risk experts, and sustainable-finance professionals.

The research contributes to climate finance and sustainable banking literature by advancing a product-level perspective on climate-risk integration. It further seeks to provide empirical evidence on the influence of climate-related risks on mortgage lending outcomes and to develop an evidence-based framework through which financial institutions can incorporate climate-related considerations into retail lending practices. In doing so, the study aims to demonstrate how retail lending can contribute simultaneously to banking resilience, climate adaptation, and the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy.

title: A Strain-Resolved Genome Resource Defines Conserved Infant Gut Microbiome Assembly across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia

detail.title: A Strain-Resolved Genome Resource Defines Conserved Infant Gut Microbiome Assembly across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia
detail.abstract: Infant gut microbiome assembly shapes growth, immunity, and neurodevelopment, yet almost all high-resolution metagenomic data derive from high-income cohorts. We assembled a deep shotgun metagenomic reference from 596 generally healthy children aged 2–23 months across nine sites in six low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. From ~5.7 Tbp we reconstructed 7,683 high-quality genomes spanning 1,941 species, including 220 uncultured and five novel core species, with strain-resolved functional annotations and harmonized metadata. Assembly followed a conserved three-stage trajectory (pioneer, transition, expansion) governed by breastfeeding and weaning and reproducible across all nine sites, and potentially host-beneficial functions were maintained despite taxonomic turnover. Against age-matched high-income cohorts, LMIC microbiomes diverged from the first months of life and carried higher species richness, with Bifidobacterium (notably B. infantis), Lactobacillus, and Prevotella depleted in high-income infants. This open-access reference anchors future LMIC cohorts and supports globally inclusive infant microbiome research.

title: One Market or Many? Property-Type Heterogeneity in Regional Real Estate Price Convergence Dynamics in China
affiliations: University of Nottingham, Ningbo - University of Nottingham Ningbo China and University of Nottingham, Ningbo - University of Nottingham Ningbo China

detail.title: One Market or Many? Property-Type Heterogeneity in Regional Real Estate Price Convergence Dynamics in China
detail.abstract: This study investigates regional real estate price convergence and club formation in China using disaggregated price data for different property types across 30 major cities. We make three key contributions. First, we utilize disaggregated prices rather than aggregate price indexes, enabling a more precise assessment of market integration. Second, we test whether commercial and residential properties follow different convergence paths, whether newly-constructed and second-hand housing exhibit distinct adjustment dynamics, and whether COVID-19 had asymmetric effects across property types. Third, we analyze the determinants of club convergence using socio-economic and property-specific variables. Our results reveal significant heterogeneity across all three dimensions. Commercial property markets display strong integration across cities, whereas residential markets remain highly fragmented, forming up to four distinct convergence clubs. Newly-constructed housing becomes more integrated over time, while second-hand housing becomes more fragmented. COVID-19 had asymmetric effects, fragmenting office markets while affecting residential markets differently across segments. Regression analysis reveals that rent, construction area, air quality, and economic development play important roles in explaining price convergence across cities. Our findings suggest that policies targeting market integration must be property-type specific, as commercial and residential markets respond differently to shocks and policy interventions.

title:
Severing the Fintech App 
The Financial Services Exclusion, the Collapsing Safe Harbour, and Unilateral Modification under the Digital Content Directive

detail.title:
Severing the Fintech App 
The Financial Services Exclusion, the Collapsing Safe Harbour, and Unilateral Modification under the Digital Content Directive
detail.abstract: Article 19 of Directive 2019/770 entitles consumers to terminate free of charge where a trader unilaterally modifies a digital service to their detriment. The Court of Justice has not interpreted it. This article asks whether it reaches the applications through which European consumers increasingly manage their money. The obstacle is Article 3(5)(e), which excludes contracts "regarding" financial services. Three arguments are advanced. First, the exclusion operates on contractual elements rather than whole contracts: a contract-level reading would deprive Article 3(6) of any operation in respect of service bundles, since Article 3(5)(a) would exclude every contract to which the bundle rule was addressed. Second, the objection from fragmentation is answered by Article 3(7), which secures the precedence of sectoral instruments. Third, the trader's safe harbour in Article 19(4) is unavailable in the financial sector, because a retained unmodified version cannot satisfy the security dimension of objective conformity under Article 8(1)(b) while operational resilience obligations bind the provider. The article then tests the justification offered for the exclusion. Article 22 of the new Payment Services Regulation carries over the deemed-consent mechanism of Article 54 PSD2 without a valid-reason requirement, a noadditional-cost requirement, or any materiality threshold. The Council's negotiating mandate contained an express Member State power to restrict unilateral changes absent a justified reason; it did not survive the trilogue, and because the successor instrument is a regulation the gap can no longer be filled nationally.

title: Audit Committees and Corporate Governance under Islamic Law: Perspectives from Libya's Banking Sector

detail.abstract: This paper presents a distinct examination of the impact of applying Islamic law on the effectiveness of corporate governance (CG) and audit committees (ACs) in the Libyan banking sector, to identify actions to enhance their effectiveness. A qualitative method was employed through face-to-face interviews, involving four groups of actors in the Libyan banking sector: board members, audit committee (AC) members, executive managers, and internal auditing directors. The findings indicate that applying Islamic law in the Libyan banking sector is beneficial; however, several participants noted that CG and ACs could face obstacles, and the rapid shift to Islamic law is likely to affect practice in several Libyan banks because of the weak banking environment. Our evidence highlights the pressing need for boards, AC members, and regulators, particularly the Central Bank of Libya, to pay more attention to enhancing the effectiveness of ACs and CG in the Libyan banking sector. The paper is one of a kind, examining the impact of Sharia law enforcement on CG and AC practices within Libyan banks newly embracing Islamic finance; this is a pressing issue in Libya because the Islamic financial system takes a different approach to CG from traditional financial systems, and due to the speed at which the shift to Islamic banking is occurring in Libya.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Household Production, and the Allocation of Time
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics, Tsinghua University - Institute of Economics, Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of International Trade and Economics and

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Household Production, and the Allocation of Time
detail.abstract: Does more affordable artificial intelligence (AI) reduce the time households devote to home production? Not necessarily. We develop a static general-equilibrium model in which households and competitive final-good firms purchase a common AI service from an upstream supplier. The supplier's fixed markup is the exogenous ratio of the AI-service price to short-run marginal cost; it distributes operating surplus, including capacity quasi-rents, to households as dividends. At fixed home output, greater affordability induces substitution of AI for household effort. Holding full income in time units fixed, it also lowers the unit cost of the home-input composite relative to the wage and expands desired output. Home-production time then falls exactly when the substitution elasticity between AI and household effort exceeds one. Changes in the dividendto-wage ratio add a third margin and can overturn this condition in equilibrium. The aggregate equilibrium is unique and recursively determined by one scalar equation in the wage-to-AIprice ratio. Higher upstream AI productivity raises affordability, aggregate AI use, and welfare. Greater final-sector AI bias raises aggregate use but lowers household affordability, and its welfare effect is ambiguous. A larger fixed markup lowers affordability and aggregate use. At short-run marginal-cost pricing, a markup increase has no first-order welfare effect; once the price exceeds short-run marginal cost, a further increase strictly lowers welfare despite the dividend distribution. Thus the sign of a marginal change in aggregate AI use alone does not determine the associated changes in household AI use or home-production time.

title: Interpersonally Comparable Utility
affiliations: and Sustaining Engineering Group

detail.title: Interpersonally Comparable Utility
detail.abstract: We develop a theory of measurement scales for utility functions, based on a generalization of the notion of numeraire commodity. Every sufficiently wellbehaved utility is denominated in some scale of this form, and conversely, the choice of a compatible scale unit uniquely identifies utilities up to an additive constant. We define a profile of utilities to be interpersonally comparable precisely when they are denominated in a common measurement unit. We study when profiles of comparable utilities exist, as well as how a planner ought to aggregate them, and provide applications to social choice and welfare economics.

title: The Treasury Signal That Lasted One Session

detail.title: The Treasury Signal That Lasted One Session
detail.abstract: On 19 August 2026, the U.S. Treasury announced an off-cycle expansion of its long-end buyback programme, increasing the per-operation maximum from $2 billion to at least $4 billion. Because seven scheduled operations fall within the affected maturity sectors from 9 September onward, the change represents at least $14 billion of incremental capacity. This paper examines whether the measure constitutes quantitative easing and evaluates its implications for Treasury liquidity support, long-end supply, and market conditions. The analysis finds that the operation is not quantitative easing on statutory, mechanical, or institutional grounds: Treasury and the Federal Reserve operate under different authorities, Treasury retires the securities it purchases, and the buybacks must be accommodated within Treasury's financing requirement. At the same time, dismissing the measure as immaterial on the basis of size is misleading. The minimum per-operation capacity exceeds the Federal Reserve's peak QE3 long-end operation size by approximately 2.3 to 3.2 times. The paper also examines the 20-year Treasury auction conducted on the announcement day and the subsequent reversal in long-end yields. The evidence suggests that the initial market response was short-lived, while the longer-term significance of the programme remains contingent on its implementation and subsequent Treasury debt-management decisions.

title: Talking the ESG Tightrope: Between Greenwashing and Greenhushing
affiliations: Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR), University of Florida - Department of Finance, Insurance and Real Estate and Imperial College Business School

detail.title: Talking the ESG Tightrope: Between Greenwashing and Greenhushing
detail.abstract: Using a large language model (LLM), we characterize key stylized facts about the context and depth of corporate communication on climate and DEI related issues in quarterly earnings calls for firms across Europe and North America. Both climate and DEI discourse rise strongly until 2021 and decline thereafter. In general, communications on climate change issues are conducted substantively and in terms of its financial impact by firms with worse emissions profiles, and are followed by subsequent emission reductions. In contrast, DEI discussions are made tangentially and in terms of their societal impact by firms with greater board and employee diversity, and are not followed by further increases in diversity. To interpret the empirical patterns, we provide a conceptual framework featuring financial materiality and heterogeneous investor preferences, where firms choose the substance of information provided to investors under varying communication costs. Guided by this framework, we use the 2018 EU ETS reform and 2021 Texas anti-ESG legislation as quasi-natural experiments for how financial materiality and investor preferences causally affect firms' E&S communication, respectively. Our model and empirical evidence point to a chilling effect of the anti-ESG legislation on firms' willingness to provide even financially material information, implying perverse consequences for financial investors.

title: What Lies Behind Investment Banking, Shadow Banking, and High-Frequency Trading? A Risky, Dangerous, Secretive, or Reputable Business?

detail.title: What Lies Behind Investment Banking, Shadow Banking, and High-Frequency Trading? A Risky, Dangerous, Secretive, or Reputable Business?
detail.abstract: Investment banking, shadow banking, and high-frequency trading are among those manifestations of modern finance that evoke fascination and mistrust in equal measure. Drawing on the academic literature and on current data from international institutions (Financial Stability Board, ESMA, SEC, LSEG), this paper examines what these lines of business actually are, how they function, who conducts them, and whose interests they serve. The analysis shows that all of the activities examined constitute legal, economically well-founded, and in large part regulated businesses whose questionable reputation stems chiefly from opacity, conflicts of interest, and isolated excesses. Investment banking is a highly concentrated business of a few large banks, with worldwide fee income of $60.5 billion in the first half of 2025 alone. Shadow banking, as recorded by the Financial Stability Board, comprises assets of $256.8 trillion and thus already 51 per cent of the global financial system. In high-frequency trading, roughly 55 per cent of US and up to 43 per cent of European equity trading volume is attributable to strategies whose reaction times are measured in millionths of a second; the costs associated with latency arbitrage amount to roughly five billion dollars per year worldwide (Aquilina, Budish, and O'Neill, 2022). For investors, a differentiated assessment follows: none of the businesses examined is disreputable per se, and none is free of risk. Those who understand how they work, who the participants are, and where the profits originate can weigh opportunities and dangers realistically — and may, in selected cases, participate in these markets themselves, whether through listed trading firms or through regulated credit funds.

title: From Caldeira-Leggett to Multiplicative Noise State-Dependent Coupling Channels for Heavy-Tailed Financial Returns

detail.title: From Caldeira-Leggett to Multiplicative Noise State-Dependent Coupling Channels for Heavy-Tailed Financial Returns
detail.abstract: Financial return distributions exhibit heavy power-law tails with an exponent near two, a regularity that has resisted a fully convincing physical explanation. This paper asks whether an open-system Langevin framework rooted in Caldeira-Leggett dynamics can reproduce the tail exponents observed in equity markets, and if not, what minimal extension of the framework is needed. We build a threebody model of coupled airline equities driven by empirical market noise and probe the architecture in four stages, with the goal of reproducing the empirical airline tail exponent ᾱ ≈ 2.04. A Gaussian equilibrium bath produces Gaussian outputs, confirming the internal consistency of the Caldeira-Leggett baseline. Direct measurement of the S&P 500 bath then reveals a non-Gaussian marginal with kurtosis 16 and a Hill tail exponent near 2.3, invalidating the equilibrium reservoir hypothesis. Driving the system with these empirical returns alone, in place of the thermal background, still does not preserve heavy tails. The additive Langevin dynamics average roughly thirty independent noise draws per relaxation time. The empirical market distribution has finite variance and, under iid resampling, bounded support, so it lies in the Gaussian domain of attraction and the averaging drives the output toward Gaussian behavior. It is also not Lévy-stable, so it is not a fixed point under convolution. We show separately that the finite-threshold Hill estimate rises under filtering even for non-stable inputs whose asymptotic tail index is provably preserved, so the measured attenuation is an estimator effect at moderate thresholds and not destruction of an asymptotic power law. To overcome this attenuation we make the noise coupling state-dependent, so that large market shocks are amplified when the system is in certain dynamical states. The core finding of the paper is that the timescale of the state variable through which this multiplicative coupling acts determines whether it can counteract the averaging. Position is a slow variable confined by the potential well. Coupling to it reproduces the empirical exponent only at a coupling strength more than two orders of magnitude larger than what leverage regressions measure, and it leaves the exponent untouched until the coupling is already large. Velocity and realized volatility are fast variables that fluctuate on the timescale of returns. Coupling to either of them reproduces the target exponent at a coupling roughly twenty times smaller, with the realized-volatility channel showing the cleanest timestep convergence. The shared-bath architecture additionally produces cross-stock tail clustering with co-exceedance ratios of seven to nine even at zero direct coupling, which exceeds the clustering seen in the data, while the collective mode and the mean of the individual stocks have tail exponents that are close to one another. All results are reported with multi-seed uncertainty estimates. I. The exponents we estimate in this paper are one-sided right-tail quantities, defined precisely in Section III. This range is consequential. For 2 < α ≤ 4, the variance is finite while the fourth moment is divergent or borderline, which means that Gaussian risk metrics such as Value-at-Risk can underestimate the probability of large moves by orders of magnitude. detail.abstract: When a large employer closes, how much of the direct loss propagates into the wider local economy depends on the regional and institutional conditions of the host community. Quasi-experimental evidence on which conditions matter has nevertheless concentrated on private manufacturing closures in Western economies, leaving state-owned operators and Asian institutional settings largely unexamined. We estimate the employment consequences of the June 2017 permanent suspension of Kori Unit 1, Korea's first commercial reactor, combining an establishment-level difference-indifferences design with a municipality-level synthetic control drawn from 245 municipalities. Neither design detects an effect on total employment. Beneath this aggregate null, the two designs recover different margins of adjustment. The difference-indifferences estimates show a significant increase in accommodation and food services and no detectable change in manufacturing, while the synthetic control additionally reflects establishment entry and exit and shows manufacturing falling below its counterfactual. We read this pattern as sectoral recomposition operating partly through the extensive margin, consistent with the joint operation of three absorption mechanisms. These are employment protection within a state-owned operator, partial withdrawal of a generation-linked host-community transfer regime, and a co-occurring tourism-development shock. The local consequences of nuclear closure depend on institutional configuration rather than the closure event alone.

title: Dissecting Machine Forecast Disagreement: Investor Disagreement versus Model Uncertainty
affiliations: Old Dominion University

detail.title: Dissecting Machine Forecast Disagreement: Investor Disagreement versus Model Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Machine forecast disagreement (MFD) does not identify investor disagreement when investors face model uncertainty. We allow investors to entertain multiple forecasting models and use Bayesian model averaging to decompose forecast dispersion into disagreement across investors and model uncertainty within investors. Model uncertainty accounts for about 73% of total dispersion and is almost perfectly correlated with raw MFD. In cross-sectional return tests, model uncertainty strongly predicts lower returns, whereas investor disagreement does not. The negative return relation attributed to MFD therefore reflects model uncertainty rather than disagreement across investors, substantially changing its economic interpretation.

detail.abstract: Upcycling is an increasingly important practice within the circular economy, particularly in the fashion and creative industries, where discarded or underused goods are transformed into products with a new function or added value. Yet, when the source materials embody intellectual property (IP), upcycling may conflict with the exclusive rights of copyright, trademark, and design right holders. This paper examines upcycling as a form of transformative recycling and explores whether, and to what extent, current IP frameworks can accommodate and support sustainable reuse. It identifies three interconnected challenges. First, it analyses the tension between the proprietary and exclusionary logic of IP law and the inclusive, resource-conserving objectives of the circular economy, including the emerging “commercial paradox of upcycling”, whereby sustainability-oriented downstream users may compete with established rightsholders. Second, it examines the difficulties created by overlapping IP rights in “mixed goods”, particularly fashion products that may simultaneously attract copyright, trademark, and design protection, and considers the role of exhaustion, exceptions and limitations, moral rights, and fundamental rights in resolving such conflicts. Third, it addresses the spatial dimension of upcycling, including the unequal distribution of textile waste between the Global North and Global South and the resulting risks of waste colonialism. Drawing on EU and US legal doctrines and emerging case law concerning the reuse, customization, and transformation of protected goods, the paper argues that upcycling should not be regarded as inherently infringing. Rather, it provides a valuable case study for reconsidering the relationship between IP protection and sustainability. The paper concludes that future IP policies should facilitate legitimate transformative reuse and recognise sustainability as a relevant consideration in balancing exclusive rights against the objectives of a circular and environmentally sustainable economy.

title: Institutional Quality in Sub-Saharan Africa: Persistence, Convergence, and Reform Mobility
affiliations: Department of Economics, University of Antananarivo

detail.title: Institutional Quality in Sub-Saharan Africa: Persistence, Convergence, and Reform Mobility
detail.abstract: Institutional reform is often evaluated over horizons far shorter than the institutional process itself. This paper studies institutional quality in Sub-Saharan Africa as a persistent economic state rather than a contemporaneous policy covariate. Using the 2025 revision of the Worldwide Governance Indicators, a six-dimensional panel is constructed for 48 economies over 2002-2024 without interpolation of missing governance observations. The first principal component explains 84.8% of standardized institutional variation, yet the balanced-sample mean rises by only 0.75 point on the absolute 0-100 scale. Five-year convergence is statistically detectable: the coefficient on initial institutional quality equals-0.0447 with a country-clustered standard error of 0.0175. Its annualized persistence is 0.991, which implies a half-life near 76 years. Rank persistence remains high, while transition matrices reveal substantial adjacent mobility but rare large institutional jumps. A grid-searched threshold near 54.6 fails a cluster wild-bootstrap test of nonlinearity. The evidence favors a model of cumulative, path-dependent institutional change in which administrative progress can coexist with persistent weaknesses in legal credibility and corruption control.

title: A Statistical Qualification Framework for Probability-of-Default Estimators: Generalized Linear Models versus Regularized Gradient Boosting Ensembles
affiliations: , Bahir Dar University and Bahir Dar University

detail.title: A Statistical Qualification Framework for Probability-of-Default Estimators: Generalized Linear Models versus Regularized Gradient Boosting Ensembles
detail.abstract: We propose a unified theoretical framework for the statistical qualification of probability-ofdefault (PD) estimators, defined as the formal verification-existence, identifiability, consistency, asymptotic distribution, generalization bound-of every stage of a credit-scoring pipeline, without recourse to numerical simulation. We formalize PD as the conditional expectation f * (x) = P(Y = 1 | X = x) and compare two competing hypothesis classes: the generalized linear model (logistic regression) and additive tree ensembles obtained by regularized gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM). For the first class, we establish existence and uniqueness of the maximum-likelihood estimator under a separation condition, together with its consistency and asymptotic normality. For the second, we show the monotone decrease of the regularized training objective and state a generalization bound based on Rademacher complexity. We then validate, through results either proved in full or rigorously cited, the standard components of a scoring pipeline: the AUC statistic as a Mann-Whitney U-statistic together with its asymptotic law, the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic, the Information Value as a Jeffreys divergence together with its local quadratic expansion linking this heuristic criterion to a χ 2 divergence, the Murphy decomposition of the Brier score for calibration, the geometric properties of synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE), and the existence-uniqueness theorem for Shapley values used for explainability. Taken together, these results constitute a fully analytically verifiable qualification protocol, of particular relevance to microfinance portfolios where limited sample size restricts the scope of purely empirical validation.

It advances a convertibility framework and a value capture framework, and applies both to Haryana. Its convertibility remains structurally bounded.

detail.abstract: In many economies, long working hours extend into the evening, delaying the time parents return home and compressing the hours available for their children. This study examines whether parents' late return from work is associated with children's behavioral problems through reduced parent-child time, using data from a large national birth cohort in Japan (the Longitudinal Survey of Newborns in the 21st Century; analytic sample of 9,458 dual-earner households), a setting in which prior evidence suggests that overtime, rather than shift work, is an important source of late return. Building on the nonstandard work schedules (NSWS) literature, late return is defined as typically returning home from work between 7 p.m. and 8 a.m. Causal mediation analysis decomposes the total association between parents' late return and children's behavioral problems at age 9 into direct and indirect components, with the indirect component operating through parent-child time. Results differ markedly by parent gender. Mothers' late return is associated with higher behavioral problems, and the estimated mediated share is substantially larger when weekday mother-child time is the mediator (26%) than when days-off time is the mediator (7%); these percentages come from separate single-mediator models. Fathers' late return shows no robust total association with child outcomes, despite fathers' substantially longer work hours. This pattern is consistent with mothers' primary caregiver role making maternal time less substitutable. The findings suggest that where overtime is widespread and caregiving remains gendered, time constraints on mothers can have measurable consequences for children. They underscore the need for work-hour policies that protect parent-child time and for measures that promote a more equal division of caregiving.

title: Auctions with Outside Options

detail.title: Auctions with Outside Options
detail.abstract: Consider a finite set of potential bidders for the sale of an indivisible object where every bidder has an outside option. Bidders have private information about the object's value and their outside option which are drawn from two different probability distributions. Every bidder participates in the auction if and only if their value for the object is larger than their outside option, which leads to uncertain number of participants. The seller imposes a floor on the number of participating bidders in order to conduct an auction. If the floor is not met, the auction is canceled. We show that if either the value distribution is strengthened or the outside option distribution is weakened, the bidders raise their bids. We also show that the bidders raise their bids due to the imposition of a floor.

title: Proper Scoring Rules for Correlation Matrix Forecasts on the SPD Manifold: Theory and Empirical Evidence

detail.title: Proper Scoring Rules for Correlation Matrix Forecasts on the SPD Manifold: Theory and Empirical Evidence
detail.abstract: Correlation and covariance matrix forecasts are typically evaluated with the energy score or the variogram score, both built from at (Euclidean/Frobenius) distances even though correlation matrices live on a curved space the cone of symmetric positive denite (SPD) matrices under the ane-invariant metric. We study geometry-aware extensions of both scores, built from the ane-invariant (FisherRao) geodesic distance, and place them on a rigorous footing. We prove: (i) a general theorem that any conditionally negative denite (CND) kernel yields a proper scoring rule via the classical energy-distance construction, with a complete self-contained Hilbert-space proof; (ii) that |x−y|p is CND on R exactly for p ∈(0,2], with an explicit minimal counterexample for p>2; (iii) that variogram-style scores are proper elicitors of a pairwise-moment vector for any xed measurable entrywise transform, requiring no CND condition at all; and (iv) a new exact isometric embedding showing the ane-invariant distance, restricted to any commuting family of SPD matrices, is exactly a rescaled Euclidean distance in log-eigenvalue coordinates. Together these results settle propriety unconditionally for the geometric variogram score and for a geometric generalization of the energy score restricted to single-geodesic (e.g. stress-ladder) ensembles; for the geometric energy score on generic, non-commuting ensembles, we show numerically that the sucient CND condition genuinely fails once enough points are considered, at dimension 3 5 (though not yet at higher dimension), and state this precisely as an open conjecture. We complement the theory with an honest empirical investigation on synthetic and real data (walk-forward regime-switching correlation forecasts for a ve-industry-portfolio equity panel): a controlled synthetic test shows the geometric variogram score detects boundary-proximate forecast danger invisible to its at counterpart; on real data the picture is more nuanced the geometric score's edge is present but smaller than the at score's in a full-sample comparison, and concentrates specically in market episodes wher correlations genuinely approach the singular boundary, disappearing in an unconditional average. We report this, and a further real-data test that returns a negative result, to characterize precisely when the geometric approach helps rather than claiming it always does.

title: Secular Decline in the Lower Yangzi Delta? Rural Wages, Work Patterns, and State-market Dynamics in Hydraulic Construction, 1827-1936

detail.title: Secular Decline in the Lower Yangzi Delta? Rural Wages, Work Patterns, and State-market Dynamics in Hydraulic Construction, 1827-1936

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Review of Economic History, 2026[10.1093/ereh/heag017]

detail.abstract: Scholars have long debated whether the rural sector in the Lower Yangzi Delta of China declined after the nineteenth century. Using hydraulic construction as cases, this article finds neither decline nor stagnation. State-elite collaboration intensified in public goods provision, while labor institutions increasingly adapted to changing market dynamics. While rural wage incomes dipped in the 1820s-1830s, they rose substantially after the 1860s and moved towards sustained growth in the early twentieth century. These findings highlight a far more dynamic rural economy and pre-industrial labor market, where laborers moved flexibly between farming and non-farm work, and between casual and regular employment.

title:
Energy Substitution, Biased Technical Change, and the Economy-wide Energy Rebound: 
A Normalized CES Estimation for Japan
affiliations: and Goethe University Frankfurt

detail.title:
Energy Substitution, Biased Technical Change, and the Economy-wide Energy Rebound: 
A Normalized CES Estimation for Japan
detail.abstract: We estimate an energy-extended Constant Elasticity of Substitution (CES) production function for Japan's aggregate economy to examine how high energy demand and low domestic energy sufficiency shaped supply-side production conditions from 1978 to 2019. Treating energy as an intermediate input and applying the "Normalized Supply-Side System Approach", we find a low elasticity of substitution for energy and a decelerating, time-varying energy-saving bias in technical progress. Our framework also quantifies an economy-wide rebound effect, an often-overlooked obstacle to the reduction of energy use that has rarely been investigated for the case of Japan: on average, 39% of energy efficiency gains over the sample period are offset by a subsequent unintended increase in energy consumption. These results are robust to extensive checks, including grid searches over initial values, alternative nesting structures, bootstrapped errors, addressing endogeneity concerns, and trend-filtering methods. Allowing for smooth technological regime shifts improves the model fit and reveals a sharp reversal toward accelerating energysaving technical progress after the Fukushima accident in 2011. Yet, the rebound estimate simultaneously increases to nearly 50% in the improved model. Further decomposition of energy inputs into clean and fossil-based components indicates low interfuel substitutability, suggesting a limited flexibility to switch toward a greener energy mix. Overall, our empirical findings indicate that Japan's supply-side structure and its technical progress are insufficient to support sustained energy-growth decoupling in the long run, leaving the economy vulnerable to external energy supply conditions.

title: Restoring Size, Losing Power: Coverage Tests at Multi-Step Horizons

detail.title: Restoring Size, Losing Power: Coverage Tests at Multi-Step Horizons
