detail.abstract: Practitioners backtesting multi-step-ahead interval forecasts (H-day Value-at-Risk and related quantilebased risk measures) with the standard Kupiec (1995) and Christoffersen (1998) tests face a known problem: daily rolling evaluation induces (H − 1)-dependence in the violation sequence, and both tests over-reject correctly calibrated models. This size distortion, and its remedy of evaluating on non-overlapping subsamples, is documented in specialized practice — central-counterparty marginmethodology filings, Solvency II rolling-horizon VaR studies, and general multistep predictiveability testing — though it remains under-cited in the mainstream interval-forecasting literature, where daily conditional backtests of multi-week risk measures are still common. We identify and quantify a specific, previously unmeasured trade-off that this remedy does not resolve: we ask whether non-overlapping subsampling, known to restore nominal size, also restores usable power, and find that for the conditional (independence) test it does not. In a Monte Carlo study at horizon H = 90, the Christoffersen test rejects a perfectly calibrated model in 100% of daily replications and over half at a 30-day step (against a nominal 5%); size is restored only near s = 2H/3, but at that same step, against a genuinely clustered alternative — a two-state Markov volatility process with unconditionally correct 80% coverage — the test’s rejection rate falls to 4.7% (s = 60) and 2.8% (s = 90), at or below its own nominal size. Conditional coverage testing at multi-step horizons is therefore caught between near-certain false rejection at short evaluation steps and negligible power against horizon-scale clustering at the steps where size is controlled. A decomposition experiment using genuinely independent, non-overlapping blocks rules out the natural objection that this is merely a small-sample artefact: power remains near nominal even at 500 independent evaluation blocks, and instead depends on the ratio of the clustering process’s timescale to the horizon H — recovering sharply once regimes are long relative to H, but remaining negligible whenever clustering operates on a timescale comparable to or shorter than the forecast horizon itself, which is the empirically relevant case for volatility persistence evaluated at quarterly-or-longer horizons. This is, to our knowledge, a previously unquantified characterization of when conditional coverage testing at multi-step horizons is informative. We derive a closed-form analytical approximation for the mechanism, confirm the power ceiling is robust to a duration-based alternative test statistic and to a twelve-point sensitivity grid over regime persistence and severity, evaluate a constructive HAC/fixed-b correction and quantify its own limits, and reproduce the entire pattern empirically on a fully causal classical GARCH(1,1)-t system for Bitcoin, Brent crude, and EUR/USD. We close with a scope-limited protocol and a full literature positioning relative to CCP margin practice, insuranceregulatory rolling-horizon studies, and recent robust multistep testing methods.

title: Quantum Field Theory and VIX Dynamics: Implications for Establishing a VIX Microstructure Systemic Risk Management System

detail.title: Quantum Field Theory and VIX Dynamics: Implications for Establishing a VIX Microstructure Systemic Risk Management System
detail.abstract: This paper is the third in a series applying physics-inspired formalisms to VIX microstructure for systemic-risk analysis. Paper I described the microstructure's instantaneous state — entropy, enthalpy, effective temperature, and Gibbs free energy computed from a single snapshot of the term-structure curve. Paper II described how a single such state evolves, modeling the curve as a normalized “financial wave function” advancing under a Schrödinger-type equation. Both share a structural limitation of single-particle quantum mechanics: a fixed set of contracts, a conserved “particle number.” This paper instead recasts the microstructure as a field φ(T,t) with a 15 variable number of degrees of freedom — contracts are created and destroyed at listing and expiry — governed by a Euclidean action with curvature, mass, and quartic self-interaction terms. This paper completes a three-paper arc—from equilibrium thermodynamics (Paper I) to wave mechanics (Paper II)—by recasting the VIX Microstructure as a quantum field. We define the deviation field 𝜑(𝑇,𝑡) = ln 𝐹 (𝑇,𝑡) − ln 𝐹0 (𝑇,𝑡) over the maturity continuum, decompose it via the Karhunen–Loève expansion—which we prove is mathematically identical to the mode decomposition of a Gaussian free field—and construct a Fock space of occupation numbers 𝑛𝑘 (𝑡) = 𝑞𝑘 2 /𝜆𝑘 for each excitation mode. Roll events and shock repricings are interpreted as creation–annihilation events. We estimate the propagator (mode lifetimes, crossmaturity information cone with finite propagation speed), the renormalization group flow under Wilsonian coarse-graining (showing higher-order modes—curvature and beyond—are irrelevant operators, providing the first field-theoretic explanation for why three-factor term-structure models suffice), and an Onsager–Machlup effective potential whose double-well structure (contango/backwardation attractors separated by a barrier) allows a Kramers tunneling rate that quantifies—rather than merely illustrates—the “financial quantum tunneling” identified qualitatively in Paper II. All layers integrate into a five-layer systemic-risk confirmation framework.

title: Kramer vs. Kramer: On the Importance of Children and Divorce Filings for Understanding Divorce Rates in the U.S

detail.abstract: U.S. divorce rates followed a hump shape from 1960 to 2015 while wife filed divorces fell from 70 to 56 percent. I use filing records to identify marital quality by gender in a model of endogenous marriage and unilateral divorce. Disciplining the model to match 1970 divorce filing moments, the hump and decline in wife filings emerge as out of sample predictions. Rising female wages drive two effects: a direct effect raising women’s divorce value in the first half and selection into better marriages thus less divorces in the second. Paternal custody explains wife filing trends. Ignoring filing moments fails to generate the hump.

title: The Politics of Plunder From Asset Stripping under Al-Ingaz to Sabotage Capitalism -The RSF Invasion of Khartoum as Strategic Sabotage (1989-2024)
affiliations: Al-Neelain University - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Politics of Plunder From Asset Stripping under Al-Ingaz to Sabotage Capitalism -The RSF Invasion of Khartoum as Strategic Sabotage (1989-2024)
detail.abstract: This extended edition builds upon the original analysis of systematic privatization and asset stripping under Omar al-Bashir's Al-Ingaz Regime (1989–2019) and introduces a new theoretical contribution: the Theory of Sabotage Capitalism to explain the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) invasion of Khartoum in April 2023. Drawing on political theories of state capture (Hellman et al., 2000), kleptocracy (Enough Project, 2017), rentier state formation (Mahdavy, 1970; Beblawi and Luciani, 1987), the political marketplace framework (de Waal, 2016), and the regime's own doctrine of Tamkeen (empowerment), the paper argues that privatization served not as economic liberalization but as a mechanism of authoritarian consolidation. The paper documents the transfer of over 110 state assets—including sovereign territory, national infrastructure, agricultural schemes, industrial facilities, financial institutions, and public lands—to regime loyalists, security institutions, and foreign investors. It demonstrates how the Bashir regime weaponized privatization to achieve elite enrichment, patronage financing, and militarization of the economy. The central new argument is that the RSF invasion of Khartoum inflicted damage consistent with pure sabotage, not a classical coup d'état to control the state. Through systematic looting of banks, destruction of industrial zones, burning of archives and land registries, targeting of hospitals and universities, and dismantling of power and water infrastructure, the RSF campaign represents a continuity of plunder by other means: when asset stripping through legal privatization was no longer possible after 2019, the same networks shifted to direct physical plunder and infrastructural sabotage. This paper develops a formal theory of strategic sabotage as the terminal stage of Tamkeen.

title: Sovereign Clinical Compute: Capital Formation, Computational Sovereignty, and the Economics of Infrastructure Control

detail.title: Sovereign Clinical Compute: Capital Formation, Computational Sovereignty, and the Economics of Infrastructure Control

This affiliation may be relevant to readers’ interpretation of the subject matter. The analysis and conclusions presented in this paper are the author’s own.

detail.abstract: Artificial-intelligence infrastructure is often discussed as a capacity problem: more connectivity, more data centers, more accelerators, more cloud access. For clinically consequential systems in capital-constrained markets, that framing is incomplete. The financing instrument, ownership structure, operating authority, key custody, portability, derivative rights, local engineering capability, and compute location jointly determine who captures the economic value created by the system. This paper extends the irreversibility framework developed in Living Cipher Analysis 001 from custom silicon to infrastructure. It asks not simply whether capital can finance compute, but what becomes difficult to reverse when a particular form of capital finances a particular architecture. The analysis separates data sovereignty, compute sovereignty, and economic sovereignty; develops a risk-adjusted comparison of infrastructure-financing structures; connects policy and capital formation to bedside, edge, regional, and accelerator architecture; and establishes decision gates for determining when external capital accelerates useful deployment without transferring disproportionate control or future economic upside. The central proposition is that capital architecture and compute architecture are the same decision viewed from opposite ends of the system. The relevant question is not merely who will finance the infrastructure. It is what the financing causes the architecture-and the future bargaining position-to become.

title: The Environmental Cost of Place-Based Industrial Policy: Evidence from Industrial Zones in Vietnam
affiliations: KDI School of Public Policy and Management

publicationDetails.detailsText: KDI School of Pub Policy & Management Paper No. WP26-15

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the environmental impacts of industrial zones in Vietnam. Exploiting the staggered establishment of over 300 zones in the last two decades, I first show that their operation roughly doubles satellite-detected industrial combustion within 5 km of the centroids. Using wind-driven variation in downwind exposure to distinguish the zones' downwind contribution from background pollution, I then find that zone operation raises ambient PM2.5 for nearby populations by 0.70 µg/m 3 , implying a 25-day loss of life expectancy per exposed person. This effect is not fixed: it is largest in a zone's early years, attenuates with age, and is indistinguishable from zero for the most recent cohort. A scale-composition-technique decomposition attributes the variation to a shift in the sectoral mix toward lighter manufacturing, rather than to cleaner production within firms or larger scale, unlike the technique-driven emission reductions documented in advanced economies. These findings suggest that where enforcement is weak, the pollution a zone generates depends mainly on the industries it attracts.

title: Money Demand stability: A Changepoint Exploration in Dependence Structure
affiliations: , University of Glasgow, University of Calgary - Department of Economics and University of Glasgow

detail.title: Money Demand stability: A Changepoint Exploration in Dependence Structure
detail.abstract: This study employs the copula technique to examine potential instabilities in the dependence structure of the money demand function. This approach allows for modeling overall dependence while relaxing the linearity assumption used in previous studies. Our results indicate that elliptical copulas are best suited for modeling the dependence structure of money demand function based on traditional simple-sum measures (Sum M2), whereas Archimedean copulas perform better for Divisia monetary aggregates (Divisia M2, M4). Changepoint analysis of the univariate time series of the copula parameter identifies two breakpoints in the dependence structure of the simple-sum measures, occurring in the early 1980s and around the 2000s, which correspond to the beginning and end of the Great Moderation period. For the Divisia measures, we identify three changepoints. The first two, occurring in the mid-1980s and mid-1990s, are detected consistently in both Divisia M2 and Divisia M4 and are therefore identified with high confidence. The third changepoint, however, is less conclusive, as it is identified at 2017:Q4 for Divisia M2 and at 2013:Q1 for Divisia M4. An examination of stability measures does not conclusively support the conventional view that Divisia measures exhibit superior stability properties.

title: NSCAT: LLM-Driven Firewall Configuration Auditing with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) based NIST SP 800-53 Mapping and Automated Security Operations Centre Delivery
affiliations: , National University of Sciences and Technology, Pakistan, National University of Sciences and Technology, Pakistan, National University of Medical Sciences and National University of Sciences and Technology, Pakistan

detail.title: NSCAT: LLM-Driven Firewall Configuration Auditing with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) based NIST SP 800-53 Mapping and Automated Security Operations Centre Delivery
detail.abstract: Firewall configuration auditing across enterprise environments remains manual and time-intensive. Commercial platforms are proprietary, expensive and provide pass or fail verdicts without Large Language Model (LLM)-driven reasoning or Security Operations Centre (SOC) integration. Published systems do not offer multi-vendor configuration retrieval, LLM-based auditing, NIST SP 800-53 mapping and SOC dispatch within a single automated pipeline. We propose Network Security Configuration Audit Tool (NSCAT), an LLM-driven methodology that normalises six-vendor configurations into a 34-field Canonical Data Model (CDM), audits them with 36 LLMs across six providers and maps every finding to the 1,014-control NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 catalogue. A Verified or AI-inferred tagging mechanism marks each finding by line-level match against its source configuration, surfacing unverifiable LLM outputs. Completed audits auto-dispatch severity-tagged alerts to Wazuh Security Information & Event Management (SIEM) and email network-team reports via Shuffle Security Orchestration, Automation & Response (SOAR) under auditor and operations access separation. Across 303 audits, NSCAT surfaces 2,231 unique findings with zero score-extraction failures, 99.34% PDF generation, 99.96% RAG retrieval success rate (a control returned for every finding), and 100% per-attempt SOC delivery. On a 100-finding ground truth, top-1 mapping precision (correct-control rate) is 27% strict, 39% lenient; 37.7% are Verified and 62.3% are AI-inferred (n=231, post-deployment). Median audit-to-notification latency is 21 seconds, six orders of magnitude below the 180-day PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 1.2.7 Network Security Control (NSC) review cadence. NSCAT is the first to measure NIST SP 800-53 mapping precision against ground truth and compress this cadence on open-source infrastructure.

title: Beyond Labour and Capital: Information as a Fundamental Factor of Production

detail.title: Beyond Labour and Capital: Information as a Fundamental Factor of Production

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to declare

declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract: Here, the classical production model (labour and capital) is recast in terms of fundamental physical inputs: energy flows and the embodied information organising them to perform physical work. Information, as physically embodied pattern, i.e. organisation and structure, is essential to all human technology and even to life itself. All production is essentially the investment of material with physically embodied pattern. Information and energy flow are shown to be substitutable in economic production of all kinds, providing a physical basis for decoupling economic growth from resource consumption. Further, investment in the 'knowledge economy', maintenance sectors and human capital (education and training), can support transition to lower material and energy intensity, meeting both sustainability and human development goals. Broadly, moving from energy and material intensive, towards information intensive economic activity, promotes sustainability without necessarily compromising growth. Suggestions are made for quantifying and motivating such transitions.

title: Generative AI and CEO Compensation
affiliations: Peking University HSBC Business School and

detail.title: Generative AI and CEO Compensation
detail.abstract: We study how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) reshapes CEO compensation contracts. Exploiting the public release of ChatGPT and cross-sectional variation in firms' pre-shock GenAI exposure, we find that GenAI increases CEO pay, primarily through equity-based compensation. The effects are stronger with tech-savvy boards and in more competitive CEO labor markets. A shock-based instrumental variables design identifies labor cost reductions and increased firm uncertainty as two channels through which GenAI drives compensation redesign. GenAI-induced labor displacement creates surplus that raises agency concerns, while greater uncertainty increases the need for long-term risk-taking incentives. Consistent with these contracting needs, firms tie CEO pay to longer-horizon performance, reduce reliance on short-term accounting measures, and increase CEO Delta and Vega. Compensation adjustments through both channels predict higher future firm value and facilitate more efficient internal resource allocation. The results are robust to alternative specifications and tests distinguishing GenAI from broader labor-saving technologies. Overall, our findings support optimal contracting rather than managerial rent extraction and highlight compensation redesign as a governance mechanism that facilitates firms' efficient adaptation to GenAI.

title: Research on Han Nationalism in China in the 2020s (IV): Why Chinese Scholars Rarely Discuss Han Nationalism

detail.title: Research on Han Nationalism in China in the 2020s (IV): Why Chinese Scholars Rarely Discuss Han Nationalism
detail.abstract: This article is one of a series of papers examining Han nationalist ideology in China in the 2020s. It seeks to explore the phenomenon whereby discourse related to Han nationalism has increased in Chinese online space in recent years, yet has rarely been treated as an independent object of inquiry within China's mainstream social-science research system. The article argues that this phenomenon does not simply stem from a lack of scholarly attention, but is related to the operating environment of Chinese social science. Analyzing academic tradition, research frameworks, academic norms, the functions of think tanks, and the situation of scholars, the article points out that Chinese social-science research has long been shaped by existing theoretical systems, modes of resource allocation, and traditions of policy research, making it relatively difficult for certain issues involving ethnic identity, historical memory, and identity competition to form independent research paths. The article further discusses the distance between theoretical systems and public discourse, and how this structure affects the explanatory capacity of Chinese social science with respect to social currents such as Han nationalism. The article does not attempt to provide statistical estimates of the scale or social support for Han nationalism in China; rather, it seeks to pose a question: when a social idea enters the space of public discussion, why does the existing academic system find it difficult to explain the phenomenon adequately?

title: Self-Validating Stability in Matching with Incomplete Information
affiliations: University of Zurich - Department of Economics

detail.title: Self-Validating Stability in Matching with Incomplete Information
detail.abstract: Firms may forecast prospective workers from data generated only when the current matching continues. Forecasts thus determine both which markets continue and which observations update later forecasts. A continuation event is self-validating when its induced forecasts classify exactly that event as unblocked. Recursive reassessment differs from absorbing removal because it can restore previously excluded profiles. In a network model, a positive-probability selfvalidating event exists if and only if every feedback cycle contains an attenuated link, where candidate productivity matters less than incumbent productivity. From the full type space, reassessment converges to the largest such event; under nonexpansive tail forecasts, the event is unique and convergence is global and order independent. With common firm values, existence reduces to acyclicity, convergence is finite, and-under strict rankings and universal acceptability-the admissible assignments are exactly the worker-Pareto-efficient assignments.

title: factor-shrinkage: Modern Covariance-Shrinkage Estimators for Factor Risk Models in Python

detail.title: factor-shrinkage: Modern Covariance-Shrinkage Estimators for Factor Risk Models in Python
detail.abstract: Commercial factor risk models (Barra, Axioma) decompose the asset covariance matrix as Sigma = B * Omega * B^T + D, where Omega, the K x K factor covariance (K of roughly 20-150 in practice), is typically estimated as a dense, unregularized sample correlation matrix that vendor documentation itself flags as prone to ill-conditioning. cvxportfolio already ships a risk model built on exactly this decomposition, with no shrinkage of Omega applied. Two shrinkage estimators with strong theoretical guarantees - Wasserstein distributionally-robust shrinkage (Nguyen, Kuhn & Mohajerin Esfahani, 2022) and Ledoit & Wolf's nonlinear-shrinkage family (2022) - had no packaged, tested, scikit-learn-compatible implementation targeting this object. This paper introduces factor-shrinkage, which fills that gap with six such estimators behind one consistent interface, validated by 87 tests (property tests from each source paper's proven invariants, independent reference-oracle cross-checks, and full sklearn conformance certification, which itself caught two real bugs). On a real 16-factor equity model, the raw factor covariance is severely ill-conditioned - median condition number 61,406 across 125 real rolling windows, still 8,508 even at four years of daily data - driven by genuine factor collinearity (a 0.934 correlation between a technology-sector industry portfolio and the market factor), not insufficient sample size; Wasserstein shrinkage collapses this to a median of 40.8, roughly a 1,500x improvement, stable across every window length tested. We also report three implementation-level findings surfaced while building the package: a numerically safer closed-form bisection bracket for one estimator's Lagrange multiplier; a confirmed eigenvector-orthogonality bug in an existing open-source reference implementation of a second estimator; and a cross-paper sample-size normalization convention that would have silently broken had the two source papers' formulas been unified under one shared helper.

title: The Economics of the AI Boom
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Economics of the AI Boom
detail.abstract: This paper asks whether the financing of the 2026 artificial-intelligence buildout, measured under conventions that are declared rather than assumed, supports the bubble classification applied to it. Four separable objects travel under the one word: an equity mispricing, a capacity overbuild, a credit structure that depends on continued growth, and an episode of rational uncertainty about which firms capture a new technology’s surplus. Evidence for one is not evidence for another. The empirical base spans 70 reconciled builder firm-quarters, 41 financing structures, 37 country-sector portfolios, 149 valuation observations of 25 mature businesses, and the NBER railroad index, 1857 to 1937, tested against two pre-specified instruments, the Greenwood– Shleifer–You run-up screen and the GSADF explosiveness test, both calibrated on the railroad record before either touches 2026. Under volatility-robust inference the record contains no explosive episode: the test rejects in only 4.3 to 7.5 per cent of simulations, against roughly two-fifths under the homoskedastic alternative. The financing results do not all point one way. Coverage of capital expenditure by operating cash flow fell 64 per cent, from 2.871 times to 1.027, and the external share of builder funding rose from 4.3 to 35.6 per cent. Yet the consolidated, firm-level return on that incremental capital, 20.6 per cent against an 8 to 12 per cent illustrative benchmark, does not support an alarmed reading: the exception, Oracle at 4.5 per cent, is also the most externally financed and lowest-covered of the five, so the credit risk is concentrated, not sector-wide. At its own unit for the first time, the run-up screen flags five of thirty-seven portfolios, firing on United States semiconductors for 24 months, though most of it is too recent to score. Treating the reported equity-round valuation as comparable to enterprise value, given undisclosed net debt, the model layer requires 62.3 per cent compound growth for four years at the median mature multiple, a rate none of 71 comparator windows achieved, though the requirement enters the realised distribution at the top of the observed range, so the broader hypothesis is withdrawn. The financing–asset-life ratio, this paper’s other proposed discriminator, is more convention-dependent: the share of structures whose financing outlives the asset runs zero to two-thirds. A register of the choices that moved printed numbers here runs to forty-seven entries. What follows is a set of dated, checkable conditions under which this analysis, not the market, is wrong.

title: Human-Centred AI Adoption for Sustainable SME Growth in Zimbabwe

detail.title: Human-Centred AI Adoption for Sustainable SME Growth in Zimbabwe
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming how small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) create value, improve operational efficiency, engage customers and compete in digitally enabled markets. However, AI adoption in developing economies cannot be approached solely as a technological implementation challenge. In Zimbabwe, SMEs operate within a context characterised by resource constraints, uneven digital capabilities, infrastructure limitations and persistent digital divides, making a human-centred approach to AI adoption particularly important. Drawing on the human–machine collaboration perspective underpinning the 5th Zimbabwe Conference on Information Communication and Technology (ZCICT), the paper conceptualises AI adoption as a socio-technical process in which human creativity, contextual knowledge, ethical judgement and algorithmic capabilities are integrated rather than treated as competing resources. The paper proposes a conceptual framework linking humancentred AI adoption, digital capabilities, organisational readiness, responsible AI practices and SME innovation to sustainable business growth. Particular attention is given to trust, employee participation, skills development, explainability and context-sensitive implementation as mechanisms through which SMEs can derive inclusive and sustainable value from AI. The proposed framework contributes to the emerging discourse on AI-enabled digital transformation in developing economies by shifting attention from automation alone towards meaningful human– machine collaboration. It further aligns with Zimbabwe's Education 5.0 orientation by emphasising innovation, industrialisation, skills development and the translation of knowledge into practical socio-economic value. The paper argues that sustainable AI adoption among Zimbabwean SMEs requires not only access to AI technologies but also deliberate investment in human capabilities, organisational preparedness and responsible digital transformation.

title: Transformers Speak Base-2: Attention Training and the Existential Theory of (R, 2 x )

detail.title: Transformers Speak Base-2: Attention Training and the Existential Theory of (R, 2 x )
detail.abstract: Training ReLU networks is ∃R-complete (Abrahamsen-Kleist-Miltzow); with sigmoid activations it is polynomial-time bireducible to the existential theory of the reals with exponentiation, ∃(R exp) (Hankala-Hannula-Kontinen-Virtema). Both place activation atoms freely in a DAG; transformers refuse this: softmax is their only transcendental site, locked inside dot-product attention. We determine what this rigidity costs. First, an obstruction: query and key weights reach the network only through softmax, so every wired softmax argument carries an unexposed scale, and single-odds heads decide only a scale-quotiented exponential theory, strictly weaker than ∃(R exp). Second, a resolution: at sequence length three, one head emits two odds sharing one scale, and a rational calibration probe pins it to ln 2 by injectivity alone, minting exact base-2 atoms 2 τ. Third, a composition theorem: a polynomial-time, machine-verified, transcendence-free reduction from ∃(R, 2 x) to zero-loss training of masked transformers with fully trainable query/key vectors. With membership this yields ∃(R, 2 x) ≤ p Train ≤ p ∃(R exp); whether the endpoints coincide is a base-change question in the orbit of the Four Exponentials Conjecture; under Schanuel's conjecture the sandwich collapses: training is decidable iff Tarski's exponential problem is. A bookend-one tied parameter, one example-is unconditionally decidable, with certified decisions 10-7 from the transcendental threshold 1 + σ(2).

detail.abstract: The research intends to study the micro-level complexities of public goods provision and access mechanism in the rural Indian village. title: Basis-Dependence in Spectral Covariance Shrinkage

detail.title: Basis-Dependence in Spectral Covariance Shrinkage
detail.abstract: Six spectral covariance-shrinkage estimators - Wasserstein (Nguyen, Kuhn & Mohajerin Esfahani, 2022), three nonlinear-shrinkage variants of Ledoit & Wolf (QIS, LIS, GIS), Fisher-Rao (Yue, Rychener, Kuhn & Nguyen, 2025), and a regularized-harmonic estimator introduced here - turn out to be six named points on one continuum: each eigendecomposes the sample covariance Sigma-hat and nonlinearly reweights its eigenvalues while sharing its eigenvectors, differing only in which divergence calibrates the reweighting. We show, first empirically and then by proof, that this shared construction caps every member of the family at equivariance under rotations of the input basis and nothing more - despite one member being explicitly designed to deliver "distributional robustness." On a real 16-factor equity risk model, that estimator (Wasserstein) is in fact the worst-behaved member of its own family under a routine, non-adversarial change of factor basis (PCA-orthogonalization), and reusing its fitted shrinkage intensity across such a change costs a median 104.5% of achievable realized portfolio variance. We then derive, in closed form, exactly what any member of this family trades off: writing the precision-matrix eigenvalue map as s(lambda) and q(lambda) := lambda times s(lambda), the first-order sensitivity of the estimator to an infinitesimal non-orthogonal basis change is exactly twice the divided-difference matrix of q, evaluated at Sigma-hat's own spectrum - a no-free-lunch theorem: the sensitivity vanishes if and only if q is constant, i.e. no real shrinkage is applied at all. Minimizing that sensitivity at fixed regularization strength is a graph-Laplacian harmonic-interpolation problem; its naive solution is numerically unusable on real, eigenvalue-clustered factor spectra, but a bandwidth-regularized version - mirroring the kernel smoothing Ledoit & Wolf already use for an analogous singularity - delivers a validated, exactly matched-strength 34% median reduction in basis-sensitivity over the best existing family member across 125 real walk-forward windows, at a real but modest cost in realized performance.

title: Study on the Influence of Government Expenditure on Housing Supply
affiliations: University of Eldoret, Southwest University, University of Aleksander, Xhuvani and University of National and World Economy - Sofia

detail.title: Study on the Influence of Government Expenditure on Housing Supply
detail.abstract: The debate over whether government spending on housing aids or impedes residential investment and housing supply remains a significant topic of discussion. This study examines the effects of government housing expenditure on housing supply in Kenya from 1980 to 2024. Utilizing a time series data regression method, the analysis employs a fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) approach, along with robustness tests, to explore the relationship between the relevant variables. The findings indicate that government housing expenditure has a negative and significant impact on housing supply in Kenya. Specifically, a 1% increase in public housing expenditure is associated with a potential reduction of 0.8 housing units supplied. These results suggest that public spending may adversely affect investment in the housing sector, hinder employment, and slow the rate of housing supply. The VECM and OLS robustness tests indicate that public spending harms housing provision, suggesting that government expenditure on housing is not being allocated effectively and should be reassessed. The study recommends that the government should harness private sector expertise and funding to facilitate the construction and maintenance of housing. This approach could potentially lower costs and enhance the efficiency of government expenditure. A balanced strategy that integrates government support with market-driven solutions is essential for addressing the housing crisis in the Kenyan construction sector.

detail.abstract: This study reviews how the performance of social security pension systems is measured across the literature. It identifies 136 measures organized into nine performance dimensions: (1) coverage, (2) adequacy, (3) equity, (4) sustainability, (5) administrative and service performance, (6) labour market and economic efficiency, (7) resilience and security, (8) welfare impact, and (9) governance. The findings show that multidimensionality exists both across and within these dimensions, and that differences in population, denominator, analytical level, time basis, valuation assumptions and uncertainty can materially affect interpretation. The review also identifies exact transformations that provide duplicate ordering information and structural relationships among measures that remain substantively distinct. These findings support the use of focused and sufficiently comparable sets of measures. The paper further develops a multidimensional framework in which selected measures are represented as a performance vector and compared using Pareto dominance. The approach identifies unambiguously inferior configurations without assigning weights across pension objectives while preserving the trade-offs among non-dominated configurations.

detail.abstract: Traditional economic and institutional decision-making models rely heavily on static, binary decision trees and frictionless utility-maximizing assumptions, completely ignoring the underlying physiological, thermodynamic, and metabolic constraints governing human behavior under stress. This paper introduces the Sond-Decision Flow (SDF v1.12.0) framework, a first-principles biophysical and economic architecture that bridges cellular thermodynamics, active inference, and macroeconomic critique. By operationalizing a non-linear cognitive override function ($\Phi_{\text{override}}$) tied to critical energy floors ($\Theta_{\text{survival}}$) and incorporating a damped somatic Hamiltonian operator ($H_{\text{somatic}}$) for affective state transitions, the model demonstrates how severe resource constraints and uncreated macro-debt drains force systems into metabolic lockdown. Furthermore, the framework establishes a rigorous work-energy equivalence (defining 1 Unit of Value = 1 kWh), exposing how traditional debt-based monetary structures impose hidden biological extraction costs on active labor pools. Supported by an executable Python simulation engine, SDF offers a robust foundation for analyzing human agency, systemic stress limits, and alternative thermodynamic economic governance.

title: The Polycrisis and Emerging-Market Resilience: Climate Shocks, Financial Volatility, and Geopolitical Fragmentation as Simultaneous Stressors - Building Adaptive Macroeconomic Frameworks for Compounding Risks

detail.title: The Polycrisis and Emerging-Market Resilience: Climate Shocks, Financial Volatility, and Geopolitical Fragmentation as Simultaneous Stressors - Building Adaptive Macroeconomic Frameworks for Compounding Risks
detail.abstract:
Emerging and frontier economies are entering a structural era of polycrisis, where climate disasters, global financial tightening, and geopolitical fragmentation strike simultaneously and interact through non‑linear, multiplicative transmission channels. As the report notes, “the resulting crisis is not additive but multiplicative” and traditional stabilization tools—interest‑rate hikes, fiscal austerity, and reserve drawdowns—“fail catastrophically under polycrisis conditions” .

This flagship institutional study maps how compound shocks propagate across balance‑of‑payments systems, inflation dynamics, and sovereign fiscal space, demonstrating that climate‑induced supply shocks, dollar‑cycle capital flight, and trade chokepoints jointly produce super‑additive GDP contractions, debt‑service absorption exceeding 50% of revenue, and persistent food‑energy inflation. Econometric evidence shows that synchronized shocks generate output losses up to 3.4× greater than isolated events, pushing vulnerable economies into debt‑climate traps and market lockout.

The report constructs a comprehensive Adaptive Macroeconomic Architecture—counter‑cyclical fiscal buffers, synthetic FX hedging, climate‑resilient debt clauses (CRDCs), parametric disaster insurance, and geoeconomic supply diversification—to neutralize compounding risks. Stress‑testing simulations reveal that deploying these adaptive buffers reduces cumulative GDP loss from ‑14.8% to ‑3.6%, stabilizes debt trajectories, and preserves sovereign solvency under synchronized shocks.

Ultimately, the analysis argues that resilience in the polycrisis era is an institutional achievement, not a geographic privilege. Sovereigns that build state‑contingent debt systems, domestic‑currency capital markets, strategic commodity reserves, and digital social protection rails can transform compounding vulnerabilities into durable macroeconomic stability and long‑run development convergence.

title: Investigating Consumer Behaviour Regarding Stevia: An Application of the Health Belief Model in an Emerging Asian Market
affiliations: Universiti Malaysia Kelantan and Universiti Malaysia Kelantan

detail.title: Investigating Consumer Behaviour Regarding Stevia: An Application of the Health Belief Model in an Emerging Asian Market
detail.abstract: Background: The rapid growth of diet-related non-communicable diseases in emerging markets necessitates a transition toward sustainable, plant-based sugar substitutes. While Stevia rebaudiana offers a natural zero-calorie solution, mass consumer adoption is constrained by cognitive risk perception, sensory barriers, and habit inertia. Purpose: Extending the Health Belief Model (HBM) with consumer choice theories, this study evaluates the structural drivers of consumer behaviour toward stevia and designs actionable food marketing practices for emerging markets. Methodology: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was administered to 123 working adults in Terengganu, Malaysia. Data were evaluated using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings: Consumer adoption behavior (M=4.10,SD=0.79) and perceived benefits (M=4.08) were high. PLS-SEM path analysis confirmed that Perceived Benefits exerted the dominant direct effect on adoption (β=0.513,p<0.001), followed by Perceived Susceptibility (β=0.347,p=0.002). Perceived Barriers had no direct structural significance (β=0.072,p=0.138). Practical Implications: We propose a four-pillar Future Food Marketing Strategy focusing on sensory-nudge packaging, digital front-of-pack dosage labeling, lifestyle benefit positioning, and trial-bundling pricing to overcome habit resistance and accelerate sustainable sweetener transitions.

detail.title: Apex Vien Predictor (AVP): A Real-Time Structural Telemetry Framework for Market Regime Classification

detail.abstract: Financial prediction systems are commonly evaluated by whether they forecast price direction or produce profitable trades, but these objectives do not directly measure the structural environment in which a prediction is made. This paper introduces the Apex Vien Predictor (AVP), a real-time structural telemetry framework motivated by the Recursive Predictive Manifold (RPM-4D) model. AVP records multidimensional market-state measurements-including regime identity, curvature-related behavior, distortion, trajectory, uncertainty-cone, reflexive, override, and recovery variables-alongside signal evaluation, permissioning, and trade outcomes. The preserved 2026 research record includes a March 8-13 baseline of 16,512 synchronized signal and telemetry observations with 790 closed outcomes, followed by validation and replication windows. A preserved combined March 30-April 10 analysis contains 27,084 synchronized telemetry observations and 1,321 closed outcomes. The strongest retained regime-level result occurs in the April 7-10 replication window: Regime 5 exhibited an 89.9% signal permission rate, Regimes 1 and 2 exhibited 61.8% and 61.0%, respectively, and Regime 6 exhibited 14.9%, a 75.0-percentage-point separation between the highest-and lowest-permission states. These findings support the interpretation that AVP generated behaviorally differentiated operational state classifications within the implemented decision architecture. However, structural differentiation did not consistently translate into trade-level profitability, and the surviving record cannot establish that AVP contributes incremental predictive information after conventional signal and gating variables are controlled. The original row-level telemetry is no longer available, limiting full reproducibility and preventing new inferential testing. Accordingly, AVP is presented as an empirically motivated structural-measurement framework rather than as a validated profitable forecasting system. A prospective confirmatory study using immutable row-level data, frozen benchmarks, and temporal out-of-sample testing is required to determine whether AVP telemetry provides reproducible incremental information for predictive reliability, selective abstention, or regime-conditioned execution.

title: It Is the Economy, Stupid: Maritime Adaptation to Trade Protectionism
affiliations: University of Macedonia, , , University of Macedonia - Department of Economics and Central Bank of Cyprus

detail.title: It Is the Economy, Stupid: Maritime Adaptation to Trade Protectionism
detail.abstract: Trade protectionism changes not only trade volumes and prices but also the operational choices of firms that move international commerce. This letter uses an original survey of 84 respondents drawn from maritime and related professional networks to examine whether reported operational adaptation is associated with perceived economic consequences of tariffs or with broader attitudes toward globalization and free trade. Principalcomponent analysis identifies two dimensions-Economic Concern and Globalization Orientation-that explain 69.2% of the variation across eight perception items. In the prespecified-response sample (N = 77), robust logit estimates show that Economic Concern is positively associated with operational adaptation, whereas Globalization Orientation is not. Multinomial estimates indicate that the relationship is strongest for port substitution and near-shoring responses. The findings suggest that maritime adaptation to protectionism is better understood as a response to perceived commercial exposure than as an expression of general views about globalization.

title: Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Economics (AMEE): Reframing the Theory of the Firm under Zero-Marginal-Labor Coordination and Algorithmic Clearing

detail.title: Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Economics (AMEE): Reframing the Theory of the Firm under Zero-Marginal-Labor Coordination and Algorithmic Clearing
detail.abstract: For nearly a century, Ronald Coase's Theory of the Firm and Williamson's Transaction Cost Economics (TCE) have posited that internal managerial coordination costs impose diminishing returns to scale, constraining optimal firm size and necessitating O(N) marginal operational labor overhead. The recent empirical emergence of autonomous micro-enterprises achieving multi-billion-dollar transaction throughput with fewer than ten employees represents a departure from neoclassical organizational theory. This paper formalizes the Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Economics (AMEE) framework, establishing microeconomic foundations for algorithmic contracting, endogenous boundary contraction, and capital-labor substitution elasticity under generative multi-agent systems (σ → ∞). We formulate an augmented production function incorporating algorithmic coordination capital, derive the marginal-cost equilibrium under automated verification lattices, prove a boundedrisk proposition governing coordination failure under algorithmic governance, and present comparative empirical evidence of a 94.8% contraction in non-settlement marginal operating costs. We close by analyzing structural implications for electronic platform microstructure, market contestability, and post-labor corporate governance, and outline a doctoral research agenda extending this framework.

detail.abstract: The U.S. manufacturing and supply-chain systems are becoming more vulnerable to a growing number of interconnected and rapidly changing disruptions, such as operational uncertainty, cybersecurity threats, supply interruptions, and shifts in market conditions, which means that traditional risk-management methods, those which usually rely on fixed assessments and reactive actions, have reached their limits. Recent research has shown that artificial intelligence (AI)-driven risk analytics can enhance the ability to identify, predict, and manage these types of risks by incorporating large-scale data, predictive models, and decision-support functions into manufacturing and supply-chain operations (Chukwu et al., 2024; Singh et al., 2024; Belhadi et al., 2024; Wong et al., 2024; Smyth et al., 2024). This study looks at the role that AI-enabled risk analytics can play in making U.S. manufacturing and supply-chain systems more resilient, with a special focus on the connection between AI, predictive analytics, risk intelligence, cybersecurity, real-time information, and organizational resilience. The combined results show that AI can help with the early detection of risks, allow for a more proactive rather than a reactive approach to risk management, improve real-time responsiveness, increase supply-chain visibility, and enable faster and more informed decision-making (Diyora, 2024; Mishu et al., 2025; Nsama, 2025; Singh et al., 2025). Yet the effectiveness of AI-enabled risk analytics cannot be judged solely on the basis of technological capability; it is also affected by the quality of the data, cybersecurity measures, organizational readiness, system integration, and proper human supervision. The study thus concludes that AI should not be seen simply as an automation technology but rather as a risk-intelligence capability that is part of a wider resilience framework combining technological intelligence, organizational capabilities, and human judgement in order to boost the ability of U.S. manufacturing and supply-chain systems to anticipate, absorb, and respond to disruptions (Beta et al., 2025; Wu et al., 2025; Guo et al., 2025; George, 2025).

title: From Specialization to the Augmented Polymath: How Generative AI Lowers the Cost of Cognitive Integration A Historical and Philosophical Account of Knowledge Production

detail.abstract: This article is situated within the history and philosophy of knowledge production and uses generative artificial intelligence as a case through which to reconsider the historical and cognitive conditions that have shaped the organization of human knowledge. Its central argument is that specialization and sub-specialization are not fixed features of science and human knowledge, but historical responses to the cost of cognitive integration, the mental cost involved in acquiring, connecting, translating, and integrating distant bodies of knowledge, which increased as the volume of human knowledge expanded beyond the capacity of any single individual to acquire and process it. In this article, this cost functions as an explanatory theoretical variable rather than as a fully developed empirical measure. The article argues that artificial intelligence may alter the conditions underlying this cost at two complementary levels. At the level of working memory, it can reduce the cost associated with translating, contextualizing, and synthesizing knowledge across domains in real time. At the level of long-term memory, it can provide broad access to bodies of knowledge whose independent acquisition would otherwise require years of learning and specialization within each domain. This does not entail an increase in human biological capacity or the elimination of the need for expertise. Rather, it represents a change in the amount of cognitive work required of the individual to perform integration across domains.

detail.abstract: Chinese autocallable ("snowball") notes generated predictable, state-dependent dealer hedging flows around their knock-in and knock-out barriers. This paper reconstructs the January 2024 knock-in episode from the hedging side. Using a finite-difference implementation of a representative CSI 500-linked note — validated by grid-refinement and bump-size checks, and cross-checked against a Monte Carlo implementation using common random numbers — I show that the economically relevant quantity is the hedge released across the barrier region rather than a pointwise delta at the contractual barrier, and that remaining tenor changes this release by an order of magnitude: from roughly 0.6× of notional at twelve months to maturity to about 6× at one month. Combining published estimates of barrier and maturity concentration with futures-market capacity, hypothetical one-way flows of RMB 5–10bn per 100 index points are small relative to stress-window turnover, while a concentrated near-dated cohort could generate RMB 22–43bn — microstructurally meaningful if executed in a short window. A 120-day constant-maturity basis series and family- and date-fixed-effect event-window regressions show basis widening and activity increases in the CSI 500/1000 futures families significantly exceeding the CSI 300/SSE 50 controls; these are consistency results, not causal identification. The monitoring framework — outstanding notional × barrier concentration × maturity concentration × local dealer gamma — transfers to Japan's structured-note market, but the magnitude does not: Japanese retail issuance is more single-name-oriented, barriers sit further out of the money, and only one of the four variables is currently measurable from public disclosure.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in the financial intermediation, yet its impact on core bank fundamentals remains empirically contested. This study examines whether AI adoption generates tangible improvements in asset quality or primarily reflects technological signalling. Using staggered AI adoption across Indian commercial banks from 2011-2025, we examine the dynamic impact of AI implementation on non-performing assets (NPAs). We document a deterioration in asset quality in the years preceding adoption, consistent with technology investment responding endogenously to rising credit risk and operational stress. Following adoption, however, NPAs decline significantly and persistently, indicating that AI deployment facilitates improvement in risk monitoring and credit screening rather than merely signalling innovation. These results are robust to bank and year fixed effects, differential pre-trends, ownership heterogeneity, and macroeconomic controls. By linking AI to balance-sheet outcomes, this study provides causal evidence that technological integration stabilizes credit risk management and contributes to banking sector stability in the medium term.

title: What a Backtest Overfitting Diagnostic Measures, and What Readers Take It to Mean

detail.title: What a Backtest Overfitting Diagnostic Measures, and What Readers Take It to Mean
detail.abstract: The probability of backtest overfitting measures how consistently the configuration selected in-sample continues to dominate its grid out-of-sample. Its authors state that the method assumes the grid represents the trials actually performed. Readers take a low value to mean that a backtest is not overfitted. These two readings coincide when the assumption holds and diverge when it does not, and we quantify the divergence. Simulating a researcher who explores M configurations with no edge whatsoever and reports a grid of ten containing the winner, the selection damage grows from 0.066 to 0.141 as M goes from ten to a thousand, while the reported statistic falls from 0.54 to 0.10. The direction is the difficulty: a wider hidden search produces a winner that is an extreme of the whole sample and therefore dominates its grid more consistently, which is exactly what a low value records. The effect holds under the Sharpe ratio as originally specified and under the mean outcome, under selection on the full sample and on a training subperiod, with and without a genuine edge, and at every level of correlation between configurations we tested. No statistic computed on the reported grid recovers what is missing. The diagnostic retains only the mean of the winner's out-of-sample ranks; their dispersion separates the two regimes when configurations are independent, and the separation vanishes once neighbouring configurations share sixty percent of their trades, as adjacent parameter values do. A protocol condition does restore it. When the grid is fixed before evaluation, the statistic becomes insensitive to search outside it, with a trend of-0.00 against-0.38 under free search. But an unverified pre-declaration is worth little: a researcher who declares a grid and explores elsewhere anyway finds a better candidate outside it in eighty-eight percent of cases at a thousand external trials, and the damage returns. The condition that makes the diagnostic interpretable is therefore a timestamped record of the search, which is a documentary artefact rather than a property of the returns.

title: The Corridor's Hidden Fragility, Applying the Reference-Class Correction to the Economic Appraisal of a West African Road

detail.title: The Corridor's Hidden Fragility, Applying the Reference-Class Correction to the Economic Appraisal of a West African Road

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interest. The study reuses only public appraisal documents of the African Development Bank and public World Bank evaluation data.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study uses only publicly available project appraisal and evaluation documents and involves no human participants or personal data.
